title.zh: 卷一百五十 列傳第三十七: 石抹也先 何伯祥 李守賢 耶律阿海 何實 郝和尚拔都 趙瑨 石抹明安 張榮 劉亨安
title.en: Volume 150 Biographies 37: Shimoyexian, Heboxiang, Li Shouxian, Yelu Ahai, He Shi, Haoheshangbadou, Zhaojin, Shimomingan, Zhang Rong, Liu Hengan
title.raw: 卷一百五十 列傳第三十七: 石抹也先 何伯祥 李守賢 耶律阿海 何實 郝和尚拔都 趙瑨 石抹明安 張榮 劉亨安 Volume 150 Biographies 37: Shimoyexian, Heboxiang, Li Shouxian, Yelu Ahai, He Shi, Haoheshangbadou, Zhaojin, Shimomingan, Zhang Rong, Liu Hengan

sentences.zh: 石抹也先

translations.literal: Shimoyexian
translations.idiomatic: Shimoyexian

sentences.zh: 石抹也先者，遼人也。

translations.literal: Shimoyexian was a man of the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Shimoyexian was a subject of the Liao dynasty.

sentences.zh: 其先，嘗從蕭后舉族入突厥，及后還而族留。

translations.literal: His ancestors had once followed Empress Xiao with the whole clan into the Türks; when the empress returned, the clan remained behind.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had once followed Empress Xiao when she led the entire clan into Türk lands; when she returned, the clan stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 至遼為述律氏，號稱后族。

translations.literal: Under the Liao they became the Shulü clan and were styled the empress's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liao they became the Shulü clan, known as the empress's lineage.

sentences.zh: 遼亡，改述律氏為石抹氏。

translations.literal: When the Liao perished, the Shulü clan was changed to the Shimou clan.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Liao, the Shulü were renamed the Shimou clan.

sentences.zh: 其祖庫烈兒，誓不食金祿，率部落遠徙。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kulie'er swore never to accept Jin stipends and led the tribe in a distant migration.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kulie'er vowed never to take office under the Jin and led the tribe away to distant lands.

sentences.zh: 年九十，夜得疾，命家人候日出則以報，及旦，沐浴拜日而卒。

translations.literal: At ninety he fell ill at night and ordered his household to report when the sun rose; at dawn he bathed, bowed to the sun, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At ninety he took ill one night and told his family to notify him at sunrise; when day broke he bathed, paid homage to the sun, and died.

sentences.zh: 父脫羅華察兒，亦不仕。

translations.literal: His father Tuoluohuacha'er likewise did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tuoluohuacha'er also refused government service.

sentences.zh: 有子五人，也先其仲子也。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Yexian was the second.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons; Yexian was the second-born.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，從其父問宗國之所以亡，即大憤曰：「兒能復之。」

translations.literal: At ten years of age, hearing from his father why the ancestral state had perished, he was greatly angered and said, "Your son can restore it."
translations.idiomatic: When he was ten, his father explained why their dynasty had fallen, and the boy flared with anger: "I can bring it back."

sentences.zh: 及長，勇力過人，善騎射，多智略，豪服諸部。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his courage and strength surpassed others; he excelled at mounted archery, possessed many stratagems, and won the submission of the tribes by his prowess.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was stronger and braver than his peers, a superb horseman and archer, full of stratagems, and the tribes submitted to his leadership.

sentences.zh: 金人聞其名，徵為奚部長，即讓其兄贍德納曰：「兄姑受之，為保宗族計。」

translations.literal: The Jin, hearing his name, summoned him to be chief of the Xi tribe; he at once yielded the post to his elder brother Shanden'a, saying, "Brother, accept it for now, to preserve our clan."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin heard of him they appointed him chief of the Xi, but he immediately passed the office to his elder brother Shanden'a, saying, "Take it for now, brother, to keep our people safe."

sentences.zh: 遂深自藏匿，居北野山，射狐鼠而食。

translations.literal: He then hid himself deeply, dwelling on Beiye Mountain, hunting foxes and rodents for food.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went into deep hiding on Beiye Mountain, living on fox and rodent he shot with his bow.

sentences.zh: 聞太祖起朔方，匹馬來歸。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Taizu had risen in the north, he came alone on horseback to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Taizu had raised his banner in the north, he rode in alone to join him.

sentences.zh: 首言：「東京為金開基之地，蕩其根本，中原可傳檄而定也。」

translations.literal: He spoke first, saying, "Dongjing is the land where the Jin founded their state; if its root is uprooted, the Central Plain can be settled by proclamation alone."
translations.idiomatic: His first counsel was: "Dongjing is where the Jin built their power; destroy that foundation and the Central Plain will fall to a single proclamation."

sentences.zh: 太祖悅，命從太師、國王木華黎取東京。

translations.literal: The Taizu was pleased and ordered him to follow the Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali to take Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and ordered him to march with Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali against Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 師過臨潢，次高州，木華黎令也先率千騎為先鋒，也先曰：「兵貴奇勝，何以多為？」

translations.literal: The army passed Linhuang and halted at Gaozhou; Muqali ordered Yexian to lead a thousand horsemen as vanguard, but Yexian said, "In war surprise brings victory—why so many?"
translations.idiomatic: The army passed Linhuang and camped at Gaozhou. Muqali told Yexian to lead a thousand horse as vanguard, but Yexian replied, "Victory lies in the unexpected—why send so many?"

sentences.zh: 諜知金人新易東京留守將至，也先獨與數騎，邀而殺之，懷其所受誥命，至東京，謂守門者曰：「我新留守也。」

translations.literal: Spies learned that the Jin had newly replaced the Dongjing garrison commander, who was about to arrive; Yexian alone with a few riders intercepted and killed him, took the commission he carried, came to Dongjing, and told the gate guards, "I am the new garrison commander."
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that a newly appointed Jin commander for Dongjing was on his way. Yexian rode out with only a handful of men, ambushed and killed him, took the appointment documents from his body, rode to Dongjing, and told the gate guards, "I am your new commander."

sentences.zh: 入據府中，問吏列兵於城何謂，吏以邊備對，也先曰：「吾自朝廷來，中外晏然，奈何欲陳兵以動搖人心乎！」

translations.literal: He entered and seized the headquarters, asked the clerks why troops were arrayed on the walls, and when they answered for frontier defense, Yexian said, "I have come from court; within and without all is calm—why deploy troops to shake the people's hearts?"
translations.idiomatic: He entered the yamen and took command. When he asked why troops lined the walls, the clerks said it was routine frontier defense. Yexian said, "I have just come from court; the realm is at peace—why parade soldiers and unsettle the city?"

sentences.zh: 即命撤守備，曰：「寇至在我，無勞爾輩。」

translations.literal: He at once ordered the defenses withdrawn, saying, "When the enemy comes, that is my concern—no need for you."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the garrison stood down, saying, "If enemies come, I will deal with them—you need not trouble yourselves."

sentences.zh: 是夜，下令易置其將佐部伍。

translations.literal: That night he ordered the replacement of its officers and unit assignments.
translations.idiomatic: That night he reorganized the command structure and reassigned the units.

sentences.zh: 三日，木華黎至，入東京，不費一矢，得地數千里、戶十萬八千、兵十萬、資糧器械山積，降守臣寅荅虎等四十七人，定城邑三十二。

translations.literal: Three days later Muqali arrived and entered Dongjing without expending a single arrow, gaining territory of several thousand li, 108,000 households, 100,000 troops, and provisions and weapons piled like mountains; forty-seven defending officials including Yindahu submitted, and thirty-two cities and towns were secured.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Muqali marched in. Dongjing fell without a single arrow loosed. They gained thousands of li of territory, 108,000 households, 100,000 soldiers, and mountains of grain and arms; forty-seven defending officials including Yindahu surrendered, and thirty-two towns were brought under control.

sentences.zh: 金人喪其根本之地，始議遷河南。

translations.literal: The Jin, having lost their foundational land, first debated moving the capital to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of their heartland, the Jin began to discuss moving their capital south to Henan.

sentences.zh: 歲乙亥，移師圍北京，城久不下，及城破，將屠之。

translations.literal: In the year yihai the army moved to besiege Beijing; the city long would not fall, and when it did the troops were about to massacre it.
translations.idiomatic: In the yihai year the army besieged Beijing. The siege dragged on, and when the walls finally fell the troops prepared to slaughter the population.

sentences.zh: 也先曰：「王師拯人水火，彼既降而復屠之，則未下者，人將死守，天下何時定乎！」

translations.literal: Yexian said, "The royal army saves men from flood and fire; if after they surrender we slaughter them again, those not yet taken will die in desperate defense—when will the realm ever be settled?"
translations.idiomatic: Yexian said, "Our army is meant to rescue people from ruin. If we butcher them after they surrender, every city still holding out will fight to the last man—how then will the realm ever be pacified?"

sentences.zh: 因以上聞，赦之。

translations.literal: He reported upward on this account, and a pardon was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He appealed to the throne, and an order of mercy was issued.

sentences.zh: 授御史大夫，領北京達魯花赤。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor-in-Chief and made darughachi of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Censor-in-Chief and darughachi of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 時石天應與豪酋數十據興中府，也先分兵降之，奏以為興中尹。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Tianying with several dozen powerful chiefs held Xingzhong Prefecture; Yexian detached troops to subdue them and memorialized to appoint him Xingzhong governor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianying and dozens of local strongmen still held Xingzhong Prefecture. Yexian sent detachments to reduce them and recommended Tianying as governor of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 又命也先副脫忽闌闍里必，監張鯨等軍，征燕南未下州郡。

translations.literal: He was further ordered to assist Tohuolan Shilibi in supervising the armies of Zhang Jing and others to conquer the southern Yan prefectures not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yexian was also assigned as deputy to Tohuolan Shilibi to oversee Zhang Jing's forces in reducing the remaining prefectures of southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 至平州，鯨稱疾不進，也先執鯨送行在所，帝責之曰：「朕何負汝？」

translations.literal: Reaching Pingzhou, Jing claimed illness and would not advance; Yexian seized Jing and sent him to the imperial camp, and the emperor reproached him, saying, "How have I wronged you?"
translations.idiomatic: At Pingzhou, Zhang Jing pleaded illness and refused to march. Yexian arrested him and brought him before the emperor, who demanded, "What have I done to wrong you?"

sentences.zh: 鯨對曰：「臣實病，非敢叛。」

translations.literal: Jing replied, "Your servant is truly ill and dares not rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Jing answered, "I am genuinely ill, Your Majesty—I had no thought of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今呼汝弟致為質，當活汝。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If you now summon your brother Zhi as hostage, you shall live."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Send for your brother Zhi as hostage and you shall live."

sentences.zh: 鯨諾而宵遁，也先追戮之，致已殺使者應其兄矣。

translations.literal: Jing agreed but fled by night; Yexian pursued and killed him—Zhi had already slain the envoy sent for his brother.
translations.idiomatic: Jing agreed, then fled under cover of night. Yexian hunted him down and killed him; by then Zhi had already murdered the envoy sent to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 致既伏誅，也先籍其私養敢死之士萬二千人號黑軍者，上于朝。

translations.literal: After Zhi had been executed, Yexian registered his privately maintained twelve thousand dare-to-die troops called the Black Army and presented them to court.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhi was put to death, Yexian inventoried his private force of twelve thousand die-hards known as the Black Army and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 賜虎符，進上將軍，以御史大夫提控諸路元帥府事，舉遼水之西、灤水之東，悉以付之。

translations.literal: He was granted a tiger tally, promoted to Senior General, and as Censor-in-Chief took charge of the affairs of the various route marshalates; all west of the Liao River and east of the Luan River was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He received a tiger tally and promotion to Senior General, and as Censor-in-Chief he directed the route marshalates; everything west of the Liao and east of the Luan was placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 後從國王木華黎攻蠡州北城，先登，中石死，時年四十一。

translations.literal: Later, following Prince Muqali in the assault on the north wall of Lizhou, he was first to scale the wall and died struck by a stone at the age of forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Prince Muqali against the north wall of Lizhou, was first over the parapet, and was killed by a thrown stone at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 子四人：曰查剌，曰咸錫，曰博羅，曰侃。

translations.literal: He had four sons: named Zhala, Xianxi, Boluo, and Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He left four sons: Zhala, Xianxi, Boluo, and Kan.

sentences.zh: 查剌，亦善射，襲御史大夫，領黑軍。

translations.literal: Zhala also excelled at archery, inherited the post of Censor-in-Chief, and led the Black Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhala was likewise a fine archer; he inherited his father's post as Censor-in-Chief and command of the Black Army.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，從木華黎攻平陽、太原、隰、吉、岢嵐、關西諸郡，下之。

translations.literal: In wuyin he followed Muqali in attacks on Pingyang, Taiyuan, Xi, Ji, Kelan, and the Guanxi commanderies, and took them.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year he campaigned with Muqali against Pingyang, Taiyuan, Xi, Ji, Kelan, and the western passes, capturing them all.

sentences.zh: 遂攻益都，久不下，及降，衆欲屠其城，查剌曰：「殺降不祥，且得空城，將安用之。」

translations.literal: He then attacked Yidu, which long would not fall; when it surrendered the troops wished to massacre the city, but Zhala said, "Slaying the surrendered is ill-omened, and what use is an empty city?"
translations.idiomatic: They next besieged Yidu. When it finally surrendered the troops wanted to slaughter the city, but Zhala said, "Massacring those who yield brings ill fortune—and what good is an empty city?"

sentences.zh: 由是遂免。

translations.literal: On this account the city was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The city was spared on his word.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔以黑軍分屯真定、固安、太原、平陽、隰、吉、岢嵐諸郡。

translations.literal: In jimao an edict ordered the Black Army garrisoned in detachments at Zhending, Gu'an, Taiyuan, Pingyang, Xi, Ji, Kelan, and other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year an edict distributed the Black Army in garrisons across Zhending, Gu'an, Taiyuan, Pingyang, Xi, Ji, Kelan, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 及南征，盡以黑軍為前列，敗金將白撒、官奴于河。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign the Black Army was placed entirely in the van and defeated the Jin generals Ba Sa and Guannu at the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign the entire Black Army led the advance and routed the Jin generals Ba Sa and Guannu at the river.

sentences.zh: 渡河再戰，盡殺之，長驅破汴京，入自仁和門，收圖籍而還。

translations.literal: Crossing the river they fought again and killed them to the last man, drove straight through to break Bianjing, entered by the Renhe Gate, gathered the archives, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed, fought again, and wiped out the enemy, then swept on to storm Bianjing, entered through the Renhe Gate, collected the archives, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝悉以諸軍俘獲賜黑軍。

translations.literal: The emperor gave all captives taken by the various armies to the Black Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor awarded the Black Army all prisoners taken by the other armies.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，從國王塔思，征金帥宣撫萬奴於遼東之南京，先登，衆軍乘之而進，遂克之，王解錦衣以賜。

translations.literal: In guisi he followed Prince Tasi to campaign against the Jin commander and pacification commissioner Wannu at the Eastern Capital of Liaodong, was first to scale the wall, the army pressed in on his success and took it, and the prince removed his brocade robe to bestow it on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year he followed Prince Tasi against the Jin commander Wannu at the Liaodong Eastern Capital, was first over the wall, and the army poured in after him to take the city. The prince gave him his own brocade robe.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，太宗嘉其功，授真定、北京兩路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In xinchou Emperor Taizong praised his merit and appointed him darughachi of the Zhending and Beijing circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year Taizong rewarded his service with the darughachiship of both the Zhending and Beijing circuits.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，卒于柳城，年四十四。

translations.literal: In guimao he died at Liucheng at the age of forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Liucheng in the guimao year, aged forty-four.

sentences.zh: 子庫祿滿，襲職。

translations.literal: His son Kuluman inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuluman succeeded to the office.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，從征李璮，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he followed the campaign against Li Tan, was struck by a stray arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Zhongtong year he marched against Li Tan, took an arrow in battle, and died.

sentences.zh: 子良輔，襲黑軍緫管，至元十七年，以功累陞昭毅大將軍、沿海副都元帥。

translations.literal: His son Liangfu inherited command of the Black Army; in the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan, through accumulated merit he was promoted to General of Manifest Valor and Deputy Coastal Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liangfu inherited command of the Black Army and, by accumulated merit in the seventeenth Zhiyuan year, rose to General of Manifest Valor and Deputy Coastal Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，改沿海上副萬戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was changed to Deputy Myriarch of the Coastal Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was reassigned as Deputy Myriarch of the Coastal Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，告老。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh Dade year he retired from service.

sentences.zh: 子繼祖，襲萬戶。

translations.literal: His son Jizu inherited the myriarchate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jizu inherited the myriarchate.

sentences.zh: 咸錫之子度剌，攻樊城，戰死。

translations.literal: Xianxi's son Dula attacked Fancheng and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Dula, son of Xianxi, was killed assaulting Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 贍德納後亦棄金官來歸，為別失八里達魯花赤，卒。

translations.literal: Shanden'a later also abandoned his Jin office and came to submit, served as darughachi of Bieshibali, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shanden'a later renounced his Jin post and joined the Mongols, served as darughachi of Bieshibali, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 其孫亦剌馬丹，仕至遼陽省左丞。

translations.literal: His grandson Yilamadan rose in office to Left Vice Minister of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yilamadan rose to Left Vice Minister of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 亦剌馬丹子倉赤，為湖廣行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Yilamadan's son Cangchi was Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yilamadan's son Cangchi served as Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 何伯祥子瑋

translations.literal: He Boxiang; his son Wei
translations.idiomatic: He Boxiang and His Son Wei

sentences.zh: 何伯祥，易州易縣人。

translations.literal: He Boxiang was a native of Yixian in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Boxiang was born in Yixian, Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼從軍于金，從張柔來歸。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the army under the Jin and came to submit with Zhang Rou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered military service under the Jin as a youth and came over to the Mongols with Zhang Rou.

sentences.zh: 太祖定河朔，惟保定王子昌、信安張進堅守不下。

translations.literal: When the Taizu settled the north of the Yellow River, only Baoding's Wang Zichang and Xin'an's Zhang Jin held out and would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu secured the north bank of the Yellow River, only Wang Zichang at Baoding and Zhang Jin at Xin'an still held out.

sentences.zh: 子昌，金驍將也，柔命伯祥取之。

translations.literal: Zichang was a fierce Jin commander; Rou ordered Boxiang to take him.
translations.idiomatic: Zichang was one of the Jin's fiercest commanders; Rou ordered Boxiang to capture him.

sentences.zh: 兵逼其城，子昌出走，追及之，伯祥執槍馳馬，子昌反射之，中手而貫槍，伯祥拔矢棄槍，策馬直前，徒手搏之，擒子昌。

translations.literal: The army pressed his city; Zichang fled and was overtaken; Boxiang grasped his spear and charged on horseback; Zichang shot back and struck his hand, the arrow piercing through the spear; Boxiang pulled out the arrow, cast aside the spear, spurred straight forward, grappled bare-handed, and seized Zichang.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiang pressed the city until Zichang fled. He overtook him, spear in hand, charging on horseback. Zichang wheeled and shot back, the arrow passing through Boxiang's hand and pinning his spear. Boxiang wrenched out the arrow, dropped the spear, spurred forward, wrestled him down bare-handed, and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 進聞之，亦遁去。

translations.literal: Jin, hearing of this, also fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jin heard the news, he fled as well.

sentences.zh: 伯祥遂攻西山諸寨，悉平之。

translations.literal: Boxiang then attacked the western hill stockades and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiang then reduced the stockades of the western hills and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 後攻汴梁，拔洛陽，圍歸德，破蔡州，論功居多，授易州等處軍民緫管。

translations.literal: Later he attacked Bianliang, took Luoyang, besieged Guide, and broke Caizhou; in reckoning merit his share was greatest, and he was appointed Military-Civilian Commander of Yizhou and other places.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought at Bianliang, took Luoyang, besieged Guide, and stormed Caizhou, earning the lion's share of the credit and appointment as Military-Civilian Commander of Yizhou and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，從主帥察罕伐宋，伯祥拔三十餘柵，獲戰艦千餘艘，又破芭蕉、望鄉、大洪、張家等寨，俘獲甚衆，器械山積。

translations.literal: In dingyou he followed the commander-in-chief Chahan in campaigning against Song; Boxiang took more than thirty stockades, captured over a thousand warships, and further broke the stockades of Bajiao, Wangxiang, Dahong, Zhangjia, and others, with very many captives and weapons piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingyou year he campaigned against Song under Commander Chahan, capturing more than thirty stockades and over a thousand warships, then stormed the camps at Bajiao, Wangxiang, Dahong, Zhangjia, and elsewhere, taking vast numbers of prisoners and mountains of arms.

sentences.zh: 察罕以其功聞，賜錦衣、金甲。

translations.literal: Chahan reported his achievements, and brocade robes and golden armor were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan reported his feats to court, and he was rewarded with brocade robes and golden armor.

sentences.zh: 壬子，諸軍入宋境，察罕自他道遽還，諸軍倉皇失措，伯祥曰：「此必為敵所遏，不若出其不意，而遂深入其地，彼不我測，乃可出也。」

translations.literal: In renzi the various armies entered Song territory; Chahan suddenly returned by another route, and the armies were thrown into panic; Boxiang said, "The enemy must have blocked him—better to strike where they do not expect and press deep into their land; unable to gauge us, we can break out."
translations.idiomatic: In the renzi year the armies crossed into Song territory. Chahan suddenly withdrew by another route, and the troops fell into confusion. Boxiang said, "The enemy must have cut him off. Better to strike where they do not expect and drive deep into their territory—they will not know what to make of us, and we can break out."

sentences.zh: 遂率兵突戰，直抵司空寨，疏布營壘，陵高伐木，為攻取勢。

translations.literal: He then led the troops in a sudden assault, drove straight to Sikong Stockade, spread camps thinly, felled trees on the heights, and made a posture of attack.
translations.idiomatic: He led a sudden assault straight to Sikong Stockade, spread his camps wide, felled timber on the heights, and made a show of preparing to attack.

sentences.zh: 既夜，命為五營，營火十炬，伏精銳于營側險要之地，天將明，令士卒速行，而鳴鼓其後。

translations.literal: When night came he ordered five camps, ten torches per camp, and elite troops hidden in difficult ground beside the camps; as dawn neared he ordered the soldiers to march swiftly while drums sounded behind them.
translations.idiomatic: At night he split into five camps with ten torches each and hid his best troops in the rough ground beside them. Near dawn he ordered a rapid march while drums thundered in the rear.

sentences.zh: 宋兵果來追，伏發，驚駭潰去，追擊，大破之，轉戰百餘里，他軍不能歸者，皆賴以出。

translations.literal: Song troops indeed came in pursuit; the ambush struck, they fled in terror, pursuit broke them utterly, and fighting for over a hundred li, all other units unable to return relied on him to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces pursued as expected; the ambush rose, and they broke in panic. Boxiang chased them for more than a hundred li and won a great victory. Every other unit that could not withdraw escaped thanks to him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，賜金二百兩。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing of it, bestowed two hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he awarded two hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 世祖南伐，伯祥參預軍事，多所獻納，卒于軍。

translations.literal: On Shizu's southern campaign Boxiang took part in military affairs, offered much counsel, and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: During Shizu's southern campaign Boxiang took part in planning, offered much sound advice, and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 贈儀同三司、太保、上柱國，追封易國公，諡武昌。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Honorary Three Excellencies, Grand Guardian, and Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of the Yi State, with the posthumous title Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Honorary Three Excellencies, Grand Guardian, and Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Yi with the posthumous name Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 子瑋。

translations.literal: His son was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wei.

sentences.zh: 瑋始襲父職，知易州。

translations.literal: Wei first inherited his father's post and governed Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei first inherited his father's office and governed Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 兄行軍千戶卒，瑋復襲之，鎮亳州。

translations.literal: When his elder brother the campaign myriarch died, Wei inherited that post again and garrisoned Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother the campaign myriarch died, Wei inherited that post as well and was posted to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 從圍襄樊，宋將夏貴率舟師來救，瑋時建營於城東北，當其衝。

translations.literal: Following the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng, the Song general Xia Gui led a fleet to relieve them; Wei had then pitched camp northeast of the city, directly in their path.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng, the Song general Xia Gui brought a fleet to relieve the cities. Wei had camped northeast of the walls, squarely in his path.

sentences.zh: 貴兵縱火焚北關，遂進逼瑋，萬戶脫因不花等呼瑋入城，瑋曰：「建功立業，此其時也，何避焉！」

translations.literal: Gui's troops set fires to burn the north gate, then pressed on against Wei; the myriarch Tuoyinbuhua and others called Wei into the city, but Wei said, "To achieve merit and establish one's name—this is the time; why shrink from it?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui's men set fire to the north gate and pressed Wei hard. Myriarch Tuoyinbuhua and others urged him to withdraw into the city, but Wei said, "This is the hour to win glory—why should I hide?"

sentences.zh: 乃率其衆，誓以死戰，開營門，以身先之，貴敗走。

translations.literal: He then led his troops, swore to fight to the death, opened the camp gate, took the lead himself, and Gui was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men out, swore to fight to the death, threw open the camp gate, and charged at their head until Gui broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，丞相伯顏受命伐宋，辟瑋為帳前都鎮撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan Chancellor Bayan received orders to campaign against Song and recruited Wei as Commander-in-Chief before the tent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh Zhiyuan year Chancellor Bayan was ordered to conquer Song and appointed Wei Commander-in-Chief of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 師次陽羅堡，夏貴率戰艦列江上下，瑋從元帥阿朮，率衆先渡，諸軍繼之，貴復敗走。

translations.literal: The army halted at Yangluo Fort; Xia Gui arrayed warships up and down the river; Wei followed Marshal Azhu, led the troops in crossing first, the armies followed, and Gui was again defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Yangluo Fort, where Xia Gui lined the river with warships. Wei followed Marshal Azhu, led the first crossing, and the rest of the army followed. Gui was beaten again and fled.

sentences.zh: 宋丞相賈似道，率舟師拒于丁家洲，瑋將勇敢士出戰，奪舟千餘艘，似道遁去。

translations.literal: Song Chancellor Jia Sidao led a fleet to resist at Dingjiazhou; Wei led brave men into battle, seized more than a thousand vessels, and Sidao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chancellor Jia Sidao met them with a fleet at Dingjiazhou. Wei led his boldest men into the fight, captured more than a thousand ships, and Sidao fled.

sentences.zh: 授武德將軍、管軍緫管，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: He was appointed Martial Virtue General and Army Commander-in-Chief, bearing a golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Martial Virtue General and Army Commander-in-Chief with a golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 宋既平，進懷遠大將軍、太平路軍民達魯花赤，俄陞昭勇大將軍、行戶部尚書、兩淮都轉運使。

translations.literal: After Song was pacified he was advanced to Far-Reaching General, darughachi of military and civilians of Taiping Circuit, and soon promoted to Manifest Valor General, Acting Minister of Revenue, and Director of Transport for the Two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Song he was promoted to Far-Reaching General and darughachi of Taiping Circuit, then soon to Manifest Valor General, Acting Minister of Revenue, and Director of Transport for the Two Huai.

sentences.zh: 至元十八年，擢參議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan he was elevated to Associate Censor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth Zhiyuan year he was appointed Associate Censor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢為江浙按察使。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was elevated to Surveillance Commissioner of Jiang-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he became Surveillance Commissioner of Jiang-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改大名路緫管。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was changed to Prefect of Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Prefect of Daming Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷湖南宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was made Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，拜中書參知政事，時宰執凡十一人，瑋曰：「古者一相，專任賢也，今宰執員多，政出多門，轉相疑忌，請損之。」

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat; at that time there were eleven chief ministers in all, and Wei said, "In antiquity there was one chancellor who alone employed the worthy; now with so many chief ministers, policy issues from many gates and they grow mutually suspicious—please reduce their number."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was made Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat. Eleven chief ministers then held office at once, and Wei said, "Antiquity had a single chancellor who alone chose the worthy. With so many ministers today, policy comes from too many hands and breeds mutual suspicion. I ask that their number be reduced."

sentences.zh: 不從，遂乞代。

translations.literal: When this was not accepted, he requested to be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: When the court refused, he asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，授侍御史，以母病辭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade he was appointed Attending Censor but declined on account of his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth Dade year he was offered the post of Attending Censor but declined because his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 七年，授御史中丞，陳當世要務十條，成宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, set forth ten urgent matters of the age, and Chengzong praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Vice Censor-in-Chief, presented ten urgent reforms for the age, and Chengzong praised and adopted them.

sentences.zh: 京師孔子廟成，瑋言：「唐、虞、三代，國都、閭卷莫不有學，今孔廟既成，宜建國學於其側。」

translations.literal: When the Confucius temple in the capital was completed, Wei said, "Under Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, in the capital and in every lane there were schools; now that the Confucius temple is finished, a National University should be built beside it."
translations.idiomatic: When the Confucius temple in the capital was completed, Wei said, "Under the sage kings Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, capital and countryside alike had schools. Now that the temple stands, a National University should be built beside it."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 賽典赤、八都馬辛等還自貶所，復相位，瑋言：「姦黨不可復用，宜選正人以居廟堂。」

translations.literal: Saidianchi, Baduomaxin, and others returned from banishment and resumed chief minister posts; Wei said, "A faction of traitors must not be employed again—upright men should be chosen to fill the hall of state."
translations.idiomatic: Saidianchi, Baduomaxin, and others returned from exile and resumed high office. Wei said, "Disgraced schemers must not be restored. Choose upright men for the council chamber."

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 監察御史郭章，劾郎中哈剌哈孫受贓，具服，而哈剌哈孫密結權要，以枉問誣章。

translations.literal: Surveillance Censor Guo Zhang impeached Director Halahasiun for taking bribes; he fully confessed, but Halahasiun secretly joined with powerful patrons and used a false charge to frame Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Censor Guo Zhang impeached Director Halahasiun for bribery; Halahasiun confessed fully, but then secretly enlisted powerful patrons who framed Zhang with a false charge.

sentences.zh: 瑋率臺臣入奏，辨論剴切，章遂得釋。

translations.literal: Wei led the censorate officials in memorializing to the throne, argued with penetrating force, and Zhang was thereupon released.
translations.idiomatic: Wei led the censorate in to plead the case, argued with sharp force, and Zhang was released.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，將有事于南郊，議配享，瑋曰：「嚴父配天，萬世不易。」

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year, when the southern suburban sacrifice was to be performed and associated worship was debated, Wei said, "To pair the revered father with Heaven is a principle unchanging for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year, as the court prepared the southern suburban sacrifice and debated who should share the altar, Wei said, "Pairing the revered father with Heaven is a principle that must never change."

sentences.zh: 不果行。

translations.literal: This was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，丞相阿忽台奉皇后旨，集廷臣議祔廟及攝政事，瑋難之，阿忽台變色曰：「中丞謂不可行，獨不畏死耶？」

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Chancellor Ahutai, following the empress's order, gathered court ministers to discuss enshrinement in the ancestral temple and regency; Wei objected, and Ahutai changed color, saying, "The Vice Censor says it cannot be done—are you alone unafraid of death?"
translations.idiomatic: After Chengzong's death, Chancellor Ahutai, acting on the empress's orders, gathered the ministers to decide on enshrinement and a regency. Wei objected. Ahutai flushed and said, "You alone say this cannot be done—are you the only man here unafraid of death?"

sentences.zh: 衆皆危懼，瑋從容曰：「死畏不義耳，苟死於義，夫復何畏！」

translations.literal: All were fearful, but Wei said calmly, "One fears only dying for what is wrong; if one dies for what is right, what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: The assembly trembled, but Wei answered calmly, "I fear only dying for what is wrong. If I die for what is right, what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾去位。

translations.literal: Before long he left office on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位于上都，授太子副詹事，遣使促使就職，復遙授平章政事，商議中書省事。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne at Shangdu he was appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, envoys were sent to urge him to take office, and he was again appointed Pacification Commissioner from afar to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne at Shangdu he was made Deputy Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household. Envoys were sent to hurry him to court, and he was also appointed Pacification Commissioner by remote commission to advise on Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 武宗至自上都，臨朝，問曰：「孰為何中丞？」

translations.literal: When Wuzong arrived from Shangdu and held court he asked, "Which is Vice Censor He?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong returned from Shangdu and held court he asked, "Which of you is Vice Censor He?"

sentences.zh: 瑋出拜，帝曰：「朕知卿能以忠直為國，朕有不逮，卿當勉輔。」

translations.literal: Wei came forward and bowed; the emperor said, "I know you can serve the state with loyalty and integrity; where I fall short, you must strive to assist me."
translations.idiomatic: Wei stepped forward and bowed. The emperor said, "I know you serve the state with loyal integrity. Where I fall short, you must help me make it right."

sentences.zh: 李守賢

translations.literal: Li Shouxian
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouxian

sentences.zh: 李守賢字才叔，大寧義州人也。

translations.literal: Li Shouxian, style name Caishu, was a native of Yizhou in Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouxian, styled Caishu, was born in Yizhou, Daning.

sentences.zh: 祖小字放軍，嘗從金將攻宋淮南，飛石傷髀，錄功，賞生口七十。

translations.literal: His grandfather, personal name Fangjun, had once followed a Jin general in attacking Song south of the Huai; a flying stone wounded his thigh; his merit was recorded and he was rewarded with seventy captives.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fangjun had campaigned with a Jin general against Song south of the Huai. A flying stone struck his thigh, but his merit was recorded and he was rewarded with seventy captives.

sentences.zh: 主將分命將校殺所掠俘，苟有失亡者，罪死，放軍當殺五百人，皆縱之去。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief had ordered officers to kill the captives they had taken, with death the penalty for any lost; Fangjun was to kill five hundred but released them all.
translations.idiomatic: The commander had ordered his officers to execute their captives on pain of death for any who escaped. Fangjun was assigned five hundred to kill but set them all free.

sentences.zh: 金大安初，守賢暨兄庭植，弟守正、守忠，從兄伯通、伯溫，歸款於太師、國王木華黎，入朝太祖于行在所，即命庭植為龍虎衛上將軍、右副元帥、崇義軍節度使，守賢授錦州臨海軍節度觀察使，弟守忠為都元帥，守河東。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jin era Dading, Shouxian together with his elder brother Tingzhi, younger brothers Shouzheng and Shouzhong, and cousins Botong and Bowen submitted to Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali, attended the Taizu at the mobile court, and Tingzhi was at once appointed Senior General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, Right Deputy Marshal, and Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army; Shouxian was made Military Commissioner and Inspector of the Linhai Army at Jinzhou; his younger brother Shouzhong was made Commander-in-Chief to guard Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin Dading era, Shouxian, his elder brother Tingzhi, younger brothers Shouzheng and Shouzhong, and cousins Botong and Bowen submitted to Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali and presented themselves to Taizu on campaign. Tingzhi was made Senior General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, Right Deputy Marshal, and Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army; Shouxian became Military Commissioner and Inspector of the Linhai Army at Jinzhou; and his brother Shouzhong was made Commander-in-Chief of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以全晉為要害之地，人心危疑未定，非守賢鎮撫之不可，乃自錦州遷河東南路兵馬都緫管。

translations.literal: The court regarded all Jin as a critical region where hearts were unsettled and not yet assured; none but Shouxian could pacify it, and he was transferred from Jinzhou to Commander-in-Chief of Military and Civil Affairs of the Hedong South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The court saw all of Jin as a critical region where hearts were still unsettled, and only Shouxian could steady it. He was moved from Jinzhou to Commander-in-Chief of the Hedong South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 既至，河東人皆曰：「吾等可恃以生矣。」

translations.literal: When he arrived, the people of Hedong all said, "We can rely on him to live."
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the people of Hedong said, "Now we have someone we can live by."

sentences.zh: 歲戊子，朝于和林，加金紫光祿大夫，知平陽府事，兼本路兵馬都緫管。

translations.literal: In the year wuzi he attended court at Karakorum, was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, made Administrator of Pingyang Prefecture, and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the circuit's military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuzi year he attended court at Karakorum and was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, made Administrator of Pingyang Prefecture, and retained command of the circuit's forces.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，太宗南伐，道平陽，見田野不治，以問守賢，對曰：「民貧窘，乏耕具致然。」

translations.literal: In gengyin Taizong campaigned south, passed through Pingyang, saw the fields untended, and questioned Shouxian, who answered, "The people are poor and straitened, lacking ploughing tools, and this is the cause."
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year Taizong marched south, passed through Pingyang, and saw the fields lying fallow. When he asked Shouxian, he answered, "The people are destitute and lack ploughs and oxen."

sentences.zh: 詔給牛萬頭，仍徙關中生口墾地河東。

translations.literal: An edict granted ten thousand oxen and further moved settlers from Guanzhong to open land in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted ten thousand oxen and moved settlers from Guanzhong to open farmland in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，平陽當移粟萬石輸雲中，守賢奏以「百姓疲敝，不任輓載」，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: In xinmao Pingyang was to transport ten thousand shi of grain to Yunzhong; Shouxian memorialized that "the people are worn out and cannot bear the transport," and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinmao year Pingyang was ordered to ship ten thousand shi of grain to Yunzhong. Shouxian memorialized that the people were too exhausted to bear the transport burden, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時河中未下，守賢建言，以為將士逗留沮撓，多所傷溺，臣請自北面鑿城先登。

translations.literal: At that time Hezhong had not yet fallen; Shouxian offered counsel that the troops were lingering and obstructing one another, with many drowned in the assault, and he requested to tunnel through the north wall himself and be first to scale it.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong still held out. Shouxian argued that the troops were stalling one another and drowning in futile assaults, and offered to tunnel through the north wall and be first over the parapet.

sentences.zh: 如其言，城果下，遂搆浮橋。

translations.literal: As he had said, the city indeed fell, and a pontoon bridge was then built.
translations.idiomatic: He did as he promised, the city fell, and a pontoon bridge was thrown across the river.

sentences.zh: 明年，蒲津南濟潼關。

translations.literal: The next year he crossed south from Pujin and forded Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he crossed the river at Pujin and drove south through Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 二月，大破趙雄兵于芮城。

translations.literal: In the second month he inflicted a great defeat on Zhao Xiong's troops at Ruicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he routed Zhao Xiong's army at Ruicheng.

sentences.zh: 時方會師圍汴，留守賢屯嵩、汝。

translations.literal: At that time the armies were joining to besiege Bian; Shouxian was left to garrison Song and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: While the main armies converged on Bian, Shouxian was left to hold Song and Ru.

sentences.zh: 金兵十餘萬，保少室山太平寨，守賢以三千人介其中，度其帥完顏延壽無守禦之才，癸巳正月望夕，延壽擊毬為嬉，守賢潛遣輕捷者數十人，緣崖蟻附以登，殺其守卒，遂大縱兵入，破之，下令禁無抄掠，悉收餘衆以歸。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand Jin troops held Taiping Stockade on Mount Shaoshi; Shouxian with three thousand men thrust among them, judged their commander Wanyan Yanshou incapable of defense, and on the full-moon night of the first month of guisi, while Yanshou played ball for amusement, secretly sent several dozen agile men who climbed the cliff like ants, killed the guards, then poured in the main force, broke them, ordered that there be no looting, and gathered all the survivors back.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand Jin troops held Taiping Stockade on Mount Shaoshi. Shouxian wedged three thousand men among them, judged their commander Wanyan Yanshou a poor defender, and on the full-moon night of the first guisi month, while Yanshou was playing ball for sport, sent dozens of agile climbers up the cliff like ants, killed the guards, and stormed the camp. He forbade looting and brought all the survivors back in order.

sentences.zh: 不兩旬，連天、交牙、蘭若、香爐諸寨，皆望風俱下，守賢未嘗妄殺一人。

translations.literal: Within less than twenty days the stockades of Liantian, Jiaoya, Lanruo, Xianglu, and others all submitted at the mere sight of his banners, and Shouxian never killed a person without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty days the stockades at Liantian, Jiaoya, Lanruo, Xianglu, and elsewhere surrendered at the sight of his banners, and Shouxian never killed without cause.

sentences.zh: 及攻河南，其渠魁強元帥者，以其衆出奔，守賢追及，降之。

translations.literal: When attacking Henan, a bandit chieftain styled Strong Marshal led his followers in flight; Shouxian overtook and accepted their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: During the Henan campaign a bandit leader styled Strong Marshal fled with his followers. Shouxian overtook him and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 秦藍帥王祐，聚衆數萬，據虢之南山，守賢使人責祐，祐素憚守賢威略，即以所部來附，關東、洛西遂定。

translations.literal: Wang You of the Qin-Lan commandery gathered tens of thousands and held the southern hills of Guo; Shouxian sent men to rebuke You, who had long feared Shouxian's martial renown and at once brought his forces to submit, and east of the passes and west of Luo were thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang You of the Qin-Lan commandery raised tens of thousands and held the southern hills of Guo. Shouxian sent envoys to rebuke him. You had long feared Shouxian's reputation and submitted with his entire force, and the lands east of the passes and west of Luo were pacified.

sentences.zh: 甲午冬十月卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in jiawu he died at the age of forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the jiawu year, aged forty-six.

sentences.zh: 子彀嗣。

translations.literal: His son Gou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 歲丁酉，從太師塔海紺布征蜀漢，有功。

translations.literal: In the year dingyou he followed Grand Preceptor Tahai Gunbu in campaigning against Shu and Han and performed merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingyou year he campaigned with Grand Preceptor Tahai Gunbu against Shu and Han and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 明年，攻碉門。

translations.literal: The next year he attacked Diaomen.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he attacked Diaomen.

sentences.zh: 又明年，下萬州，會戰於瞿塘，獲戰艦千餘艘。

translations.literal: The year after that he took Wanzhou, joined battle at Qutang, and captured more than a thousand warships.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he took Wanzhou, fought at Qutang Gorge, and captured more than a thousand warships.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，朝行在所，授河東道行軍萬戶，兼緫管。

translations.literal: In xinchou he attended the mobile court and was appointed Campaign Myriarch of the Hedong Circuit, concurrently Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year he attended the mobile court and was made Campaign Myriarch of the Hedong Circuit with concurrent overall command.

sentences.zh: 己巳，進兵攻成都，由廣元出葭萌，度木瓜坡。

translations.literal: In jisi he advanced to attack Chengdu, marched out from Guangyuan through Jiameng, and crossed Mugua Slope.
translations.idiomatic: In the jisi year he advanced on Chengdu, marched from Guangyuan through Jiameng, and crossed Mugua Slope.

sentences.zh: 蜀之餘孽團聚為梗，聞彀至，潛為伏以待。

translations.literal: The remnant rebels of Shu gathered as a obstruction; hearing Gou was coming, they secretly set an ambush to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu loyalists had banded together to block his path. Hearing Gou was coming, they laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 彀諜知之，令衆銜枚疾進，出其不意，賊兵敗走，長驅至成都，破之。

translations.literal: Gou's spies learned of it; he ordered the troops to advance swiftly with gags in their mouths, struck where they did not expect, the rebels were defeated and fled, and he drove straight to Chengdu and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Gou's scouts discovered the trap. He ordered a silent forced march, struck by surprise, routed the rebels, and swept on to storm Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 壬子，襲嘉定。

translations.literal: In renzi he raided Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: In the renzi year he raided Jiading.

sentences.zh: 戊午秋，憲宗南伐。

translations.literal: In the autumn of wuwu Emperor Xianzong campaigned south.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the wuwu year Emperor Xianzong marched south.

sentences.zh: 己未，入梁州，師次江上，造舟為梁，以通援兵，且斷宋人往來之路。

translations.literal: In jiwei he entered Liangzhou; the army halted on the river, built boats into a bridge to bring up reinforcements, and also cut the Song route of travel back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year he entered Liangzhou. The army halted on the river, built a pontoon bridge to bring up reinforcements, and cut Song communications.

sentences.zh: 會江漲，梁中絕，宋將率舟師萬艘逆戰，彀以一旅先犯之，諸軍繼進，遂破之。

translations.literal: When the river swelled the bridge was broken; a Song general led ten thousand warships to meet them in battle; Gou with one brigade struck first, the armies followed, and they were broken.
translations.idiomatic: When the river rose the bridge broke. A Song general brought ten thousand warships to meet them. Gou led one brigade in the first assault, the rest of the army followed, and the Song fleet was shattered.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝召謂諸將曰：「汝輩平日自負鷙勇，及臨敵，不能為朕立尺寸功。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor summoned the generals and said, "You usually boast of fierce courage, yet facing the enemy you cannot win the slightest merit for me.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor summoned his generals and said, "You boast of your fierceness every day, yet in battle you win me not a single inch of ground.

sentences.zh: 獨李彀身犯矢石，摧鋒陷陣，視敵篾如，言勇者，如彀乃可耳。」

translations.literal: Only Li Gou himself braved arrows and stones, shattered the enemy front and broke their formations, regarded the foe as straw—when one speaks of the brave, only one like Gou will do."
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Gou braved arrow and stone, broke the enemy line, and treated the foe like straw. When I speak of courage, I mean a man like Gou."

sentences.zh: 賜白金二百五十兩。

translations.literal: He was granted two hundred and fifty taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was awarded two hundred and fifty taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，改河東路緫管，佩金虎符，移京兆路，加昭勇大將軍，未幾，轉洺磁路。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he was changed to Prefect of the Hedong Circuit, bore a golden tiger tally, was transferred to the Jingzhao Circuit, advanced to Manifest Valor General, and before long moved to the Luoci Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Zhongtong year he became Prefect of the Hedong Circuit with a golden tiger tally, was transferred to Jingzhao Circuit and promoted to Manifest Valor General, and soon after moved to the Luoci Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至元七年正月卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Zhiyuan he died at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the seventh Zhiyuan year, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子十一人。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons.

sentences.zh: 伯溫，見忠義傳。

translations.literal: Bowen is treated in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen is treated in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 耶律阿海

translations.literal: Yelu Ahai
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Ahai

sentences.zh: 耶律阿海，遼之故族也。

translations.literal: Yelu Ahai was of the old clan of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Ahai belonged to an old Liao clan.

sentences.zh: 金桓州尹撒八兒之孫，尚書奏事官脫迭兒之子也。

translations.literal: He was grandson of Sabar, Jin prefect of Huanzhou, and son of Tuodier, memorial-presenting officer of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was grandson of Sabar, former Jin prefect of Huanzhou, and son of Tuodier, a memorial-presenting officer of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 阿海天資雄毅，勇略過人，尤善騎射，通諸國語。

translations.literal: Ahai was by nature bold and resolute, his courage and stratagems surpassing others; he especially excelled at mounted archery and knew the languages of many states.
translations.idiomatic: Ahai was naturally bold and resolute, braver and shrewder than his peers, a superb horseman and archer who spoke many languages.

sentences.zh: 金季，選使王可汗，見太祖姿貌異常，因進言：「金國不治戎備，俗日侈肆，亡可立待。」

translations.literal: Late in the Jin he was chosen envoy to Ong Khan; seeing the Taizu's extraordinary bearing, he therefore advanced the counsel, "The Jin state does not maintain military readiness, its customs grow daily extravagant, and its fall can be awaited at once."
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jin he was sent as envoy to Ong Khan. Struck by Taizu's extraordinary bearing, he said, "The Jin neglect their defenses, their customs grow more extravagant by the day, and their fall can come at any moment."

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「汝肯臣我，以何為信？」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said, "If you are willing to serve me, by what shall I trust you?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was pleased and asked, "If you will serve me, what pledge will you give?"

sentences.zh: 阿海對曰：「願以子弟為質。」

translations.literal: Ahai answered, "I am willing to offer my younger kinsmen as hostages."
translations.idiomatic: Ahai answered, "I will leave my younger kinsmen as hostages."

sentences.zh: 明年，復出使，與弟禿花俱往，慰勞加厚，遂以禿花為質，直宿衛。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as envoy again, went together with his younger brother Tuhua, was received with added favor and consolation, and Tuhua was then left as hostage on palace night guard.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he went out again with his brother Tuhua. Taizu received them with exceptional favor and kept Tuhua as hostage in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 阿海得參預機謀，出入戰陣，常在左右。

translations.literal: Ahai was able to take part in secret plans, went in and out of the battle lines, and was constantly at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Ahai took part in secret councils, fought in every campaign, and was constantly at Taizu's side.

sentences.zh: 歲壬戌，王可汗叛盟，謀襲太祖。

translations.literal: In the year renxu Ong Khan broke the alliance and plotted to surprise the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the renxu year Ong Khan broke the alliance and plotted to ambush Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖與宗親大臣同休戚者，飲辨屯河水為盟，阿海兄弟皆預焉。

translations.literal: The Taizu with kinsmen and great ministers who shared his weal and woe drank the waters of the Onon and Kerulen as a covenant; the Ahai brothers were both present.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and the kinsmen and ministers who shared his fortunes drank the waters of the Onon and Kerulen in covenant, and the Ahai brothers were among them.

sentences.zh: 既敗王可汗，金人訝其使久不還，拘家屬于瀛。

translations.literal: After Ong Khan was defeated, the Jin wondered that their envoy had long not returned and detained his family at Ying.
translations.idiomatic: After Ong Khan's defeat the Jin wondered why their envoy had not returned and detained his family at Ying.

sentences.zh: 阿海殊不介意，攻戰愈厲，帝聞之，妻以貴臣之女，給戶，俾食其賦。

translations.literal: Ahai paid it no heed whatsoever and fought all the more fiercely; the emperor, hearing of it, gave him a daughter of a noble minister in marriage, granted households, and enabled him to live on their tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: Ahai paid no heed and fought all the harder. When Taizu heard of it, he gave Ahai a noble's daughter in marriage, granted him households, and let him live on their taxes.

sentences.zh: 癸亥冬，進攻西夏諸國，累有功。

translations.literal: In the winter of guihai he advanced against the states of Western Xia and repeatedly performed merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the guihai year he campaigned against Western Xia and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，帝建龍旂，即大位，敕左帥闍別略地漢南，阿海為先鋒。

translations.literal: In bingyin the emperor raised the dragon banner and took the great throne, ordered the left commander Jebe to overrun the lands south of the Han, and made Ahai vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingyin year Taizu raised the dragon banner and took the throne. He ordered the left commander Jebe to overrun the lands south of the Han and made Ahai his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 辛未，破烏沙堡，鏖戰宣平，大捷澮河，遂出居庸，耀兵燕北。

translations.literal: In xinwei he broke Wusha Fort, fought fiercely at Xuanping, won a great victory at the Hui River, then came out through Juyong and displayed his army's might in northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei year he stormed Wusha Fort, fought fiercely at Xuanping, won a great victory on the Hui River, passed through Juyong, and displayed his strength across northern Yan.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，拔宣德、德興，乘勝次北口，闍別攻下紫荊關。

translations.literal: In guiyou he took Xuande and Dexing, pressed the victory to halt at Beikou, and Jebe took Zijing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiyou year he took Xuande and Dexing, pressed on to Beikou, and Jebe captured Zijing Pass.

sentences.zh: 阿海奏曰：「好生乃聖人之大德也。

translations.literal: Ahai memorialized, saying, "Cherishing life is the great virtue of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: Ahai memorialized, "Cherishing life is the supreme virtue of the sage.

sentences.zh: 興創之始，願止殺掠，以應天心。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of founding the state, I beg that killing and plunder be halted to accord with Heaven's heart."
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the realm, I beg that killing and plunder be halted to answer Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 遂分兵略燕南、山東諸郡，還駐燕之近郊。

translations.literal: Troops were then divided to overrun the commanderies of southern Yan and Shandong, and they returned to encamp in the suburbs near Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The army then overran the prefectures of southern Yan and Shandong and returned to camp near Yan's capital.

sentences.zh: 金主懼，請和，諭其使曰：「阿海妻子，何故拘繫弗遣？」

translations.literal: The Jin ruler was afraid and sought peace, instructing his envoy, "Why are Ahai's wife and children detained and not sent back?"
translations.idiomatic: The Jin ruler, afraid, sued for peace and told his envoy, "Why are Ahai's wife and children still detained?"

sentences.zh: 即送來歸。

translations.literal: They were at once sent back.
translations.idiomatic: They were sent back at once.

sentences.zh: 師還，出塞。

translations.literal: The army returned and went beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，金人走汴，阿海以功拜太師，行中書省事；

translations.literal: In jiaxu the Jin fled to Bian; for his merit Ahai was appointed Grand Preceptor and Acting Central Secretariat affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year the Jin fled to Bian. For his merit Ahai was made Grand Preceptor with acting charge of Central Secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 封禿花為太傅、濮國公，每宴享，必賜坐。

translations.literal: Tuhua was enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and Duke of the Pu State, and at every feast a seat was invariably granted him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhua was enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and Duke of Pu, and at every feast was given a seat of honor.

sentences.zh: 命禿花從木華黎取中原。

translations.literal: Tuhua was ordered to follow Muqali in taking the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhua was ordered to follow Muqali in conquering the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 阿海從帝攻西域，俘其酋長只闌禿，下蒲華、尋斯干等城，留監尋斯干，專任撫綏之責。

translations.literal: Ahai followed the emperor in attacking the Western Regions, captured their chieftain Zhalantu, took the cities of Buhua, Xingsigan, and others, remained to oversee Xingsigan, and was solely charged with pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Ahai followed Taizu west, captured the chieftain Zhalantu, took Buhua, Xingsigan, and other cities, and remained at Xingsigan with sole charge of pacification.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾薨于位，年七十三。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness in office at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness in office, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，追封忠武公。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Loyal Valor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth Zhiyuan year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Loyal Valor.

sentences.zh: 子三人：長忙古台，次綿思哥，次捏兒哥。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest Mangutai, next Miansige, next Nierge.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Mangutai, Miansige, and Nierge.

sentences.zh: 忙古台在太祖時，為御史大夫，佩虎符，監戰左副元帥官、金紫光祿大夫，管領契丹漢軍，守中都，招安水泊等處，卒，無子。

translations.literal: Under the Taizu, Mangutai was Censor-in-Chief, bore a tiger tally, supervised the Left Deputy Marshal in battle, was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, commanded Khitan and Han armies, guarded Zhongdu, pacified the marshlands and other places, died, and had no son.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu, Mangutai was Censor-in-Chief with a tiger tally, supervised the Left Deputy Marshal in battle, commanded Khitan and Han forces, garrisoned Zhongdu, pacified the marshlands, died without issue.

sentences.zh: 捏兒哥在太祖時，佩虎符，為右丞，行省遼東。

translations.literal: Under the Taizu, Nierge bore a tiger tally, was Right Chancellor, and acted as Branch Secretariat of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu, Nierge bore a tiger tally, served as Right Chancellor of the Liaodong Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 萬奴叛，舉家遇害。

translations.literal: When Wannu rebelled, his whole family was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wannu rebelled, his entire family was slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 綿思哥襲太師，監尋斯干城，久之，請還內郡，守中都路也可達魯花赤，佩虎符，卒。

translations.literal: Miansige inherited the Grand Preceptorship, oversaw the city of Xingsigan, and after a long time requested return to the inner commanderies, guarded Zhongdu Circuit as yeke darughachi, bore a tiger tally, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Miansige inherited the Grand Preceptorship and oversaw Xingsigan. Long afterward he asked to return inland, served as yeke darughachi of Zhongdu Circuit with a tiger tally, and died.

sentences.zh: 子二人：買哥，通諸國語，太祖時為奉御，賜只孫服，襲其父中都之職。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Maige, who knew the languages of many states, was an attendant under the Taizu, was granted zisun robes, and inherited his father's post at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons. Maige spoke many languages, served Taizu as an attendant, was granted zisun robes, and inherited his father's post at Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 時供億浩繁，屢貸于民，買哥悉以私帑償之，事聞，賜銀萬兩。

translations.literal: At that time supplies were vast and repeatedly borrowed from the people; Maige repaid all from his private treasury; when this was reported, ten thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies were heavy and the government repeatedly borrowed from the people. Maige repaid every debt from his private purse. When the court heard of it, he was awarded ten thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 戊午，從攻蜀，師次釣魚山，卒于軍。

translations.literal: In wuwu he followed the attack on Shu; the army halted at Diaoyu Mountain and he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year he campaigned against Shu. The army halted at Diaoyu Mountain and he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 妻移剌氏，以哀毀卒，特贈貞靜。

translations.literal: His wife of the Yila clan died from grief and self-mortification and was specially granted the posthumous title Chaste and Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: His wife of the Yila clan died of grief and was posthumously titled Chaste and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 子七人：老哥，歷提刑按察使，入為中書左丞。

translations.literal: He had seven sons: Laoge, who served as Surveillance Commissioner of Punitive Investigation and entered office as Left Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons. Laoge rose from Surveillance Commissioner of Punitive Investigation to Left Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 驢馬，備宿衛，為必闍赤，仕至右衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Lüma served in the palace guard, was a bitchigchi, and rose to Commander of the Right Guard's Personal Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lüma served in the palace guard as a bitchigchi and rose to Commander of the Right Guard's Personal Army.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年，世祖宴于柳林，命驢馬居其父位次，賜只孫服。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan Shizu feasted at Willow Grove, ordered Lüma to take his father's seat, and granted zisun robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth Zhiyuan year Shizu feasted at Willow Grove, seated Lüma in his father's place, and granted him zisun robes.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，戍哈丹禿，有戰功，以老乞骸骨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he garrisoned Hadantu, performed military merit, and on account of age requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he garrisoned Hadantu, won distinction in battle, and retired on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 子六人：五臺奴，襲職；

translations.literal: He had six sons: Wutainu inherited the post;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Wutainu inherited his office;

sentences.zh: 拔都兒，中書右丞；

translations.literal: Badu'er, Right Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Badu'er became Right Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 文謙，興國路緫管；

translations.literal: Wenqian, Prefect of Xingguo Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian, Prefect of Xingguo Circuit;

sentences.zh: 卜花，早卒；

translations.literal: Buhua, died young;
translations.idiomatic: Buhua died young;

sentences.zh: 蒙古不花，荊湖北道宣慰使；

translations.literal: Menggubuhua, Pacification Commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Menggubuhua, Pacification Commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit;

sentences.zh: 虎都不花，一名文炳，湖州同知；

translations.literal: Hudubuhua, also named Wenbing, Vice Prefect of Huzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Hudubuhua, also called Wenbing, Vice Prefect of Huzhou;

sentences.zh: 萬奴，為人匠副緫管。

translations.literal: Wannu, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Artisans.
translations.idiomatic: Wannu, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Artisans.

sentences.zh: 何實字誠卿，其先北京人。

translations.literal: He Shi, style name Qingqing, was by ancestry a man of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: He Shi, styled Qingqing, came of a Beijing family.

sentences.zh: 曾祖摶霄，雄於貲，好施與，鄉里以善人稱。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tuanxiao was powerful in wealth, fond of giving and sharing, and the neighborhood called him a good man.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tuanxiao was wealthy and generous, and neighbors knew him as a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 祖鼎敬。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Dingjing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Dingjing.

sentences.zh: 父道忠，仕金，為北京留守。

translations.literal: His father Daozhong served the Jin and was garrison commander of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daozhong served the Jin dynasty as garrison commander of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 實少孤，依叔父居，氣節不凡，家人常入卧內，見一青蛇蜿蜒衣被中，駭而視之，乃實也。

translations.literal: Shi lost his father young and lived with his uncle; his spirit was uncommon. Family members often entered the bedchamber and saw a green snake winding among the bedding; startled, they looked closer—and it was Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He Shi was orphaned young and raised by his uncle. Even as a boy his bearing was extraordinary. Household members once entered his chamber and saw what looked like a green serpent coiled in the bedding; terrified, they looked again—it was only Shi himself.

sentences.zh: 及長，通諸國譯語，驍勇善騎射，倜儻不羈，遠近之民，慕其雄略，咸歸心焉。

translations.literal: When grown, he knew the interpreter languages of many states, was fierce and brave and skilled in mounted archery, free-spirited and unrestrained; people near and far admired his bold strategy and all gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he mastered the languages of many countries, fought with courage, excelled at horse and bow, and carried himself with bold independence. People near and far admired his strategic mind, and many rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 歲乙亥，中原盜起。

translations.literal: In the yihai year, bandits rose in the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: In the yihai year rebellion broke out across the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 錦州張鯨，自立為臨海郡王，遣使納款于太祖，尋以叛伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing of Jinzhou declared himself Prince of Linhai Prefecture, sent envoys to submit to Taizu, and soon was executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing of Jinzhou declared himself Prince of Linhai and sent envoys to submit to Taizu; he was soon executed after rebelling again.

sentences.zh: 鯨弟致，初以叛謀於實，實厲聲叱曰：「天之曆數在朔方，汝等恣為不軌，徒自斃耳。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jing's younger brother Zhi at first plotted rebellion with Shi; Shi shouted him down harshly: "Heaven's mandate lies in the northern frontier—you who indulge in rebellion will only destroy yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing's younger brother Zhi first tried to draw Shi into rebellion. Shi rebuked him sharply: "Heaven's mandate rests with the north. If you persist in treason, you will only bring death on yourselves."

sentences.zh: 乃籍戶口一萬，募兵三千，丙子春，來歸。

translations.literal: Then he registered ten thousand households, recruited three thousand troops, and in the spring of bingzi came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he registered ten thousand households, raised three thousand soldiers, and in the spring of bingzi submitted to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 大將木華黎與論兵事，奇變百出，拊髀欣躍，大加稱賞，遂引見太祖，獻軍民之數。

translations.literal: General Muqali discussed military affairs with him; stratagems poured forth in endless variation; slapping his thigh, he leaped for joy and praised him greatly, then presented him to Taizu and offered the count of troops and households.
translations.idiomatic: When General Muqali discussed strategy with him, Shi unfolded plan after ingenious plan. Muqali slapped his thigh and leaped up in delight, praising him lavishly. He then presented Shi to Taizu and reported the numbers of soldiers and civilians under his command.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜鞘劍一，命從木華黎選充前鋒。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, granted one sheathed sword, and ordered him to follow Muqali as a selected vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, bestowed a sheathed sword, and ordered him to serve under Muqali on the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 時張致復據錦州，實與賊遇於神水縣，挺身陷陣，殊死戰，殺三百餘人，獲戰馬兵械甚衆，木華黎奏賜鞍馬弓矢以勵之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Zhi again held Jinzhou; Shi encountered the rebels at Shenshui County, threw himself into the formation, fought a battle to the death, killed more than three hundred men, and captured a great many war horses and weapons; Muqali memorialized to bestow saddle horses, bows, and arrows as reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhi seized Jinzhou again, Shi met the rebels at Shenshui County. He plunged into the fray and fought desperately, killing more than three hundred men and capturing many horses and arms. Muqali memorialized for saddles, horses, bows, and arrows to honor him.

sentences.zh: 以功，為帳前軍馬都彈壓。

translations.literal: For merit he was made commander who suppresses the army and horses before the tent.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard Horse and Army.

sentences.zh: 詔封木華黎太師、國王，東下齊數郡。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Muqali as Grand Preceptor and Prince, and he marched east to several Qi commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Muqali Grand Preceptor and Prince, and he marched east against several prefectures of Qi.

sentences.zh: 使實帥師四千，取燕南、齊西之地，首擊邢州，徇趙郡，取魏鄴，下博關，襲曹、濮、恩、德、泰安、濟寧，勢如破竹。

translations.literal: Shi was sent to command four thousand troops to take the lands of southern Yan and western Qi: first striking Xingzhou, sweeping Zhao Commandery, taking Weiye, capturing Boguan, and raiding Cao, Pu, En, De, Tai'an, and Jining—the momentum like splitting bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was ordered to lead four thousand men to conquer southern Yan and western Qi. He struck Xingzhou first, swept through Zhao Commandery, took Weiye, seized Boguan, and stormed Cao, Pu, En, De, Tai'an, and Jining—advancing as if splitting bamboo.

sentences.zh: 薄濰州，與木華黎會。

translations.literal: Pressing near Weizhou, he joined Muqali.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed toward Weizhou and rendezvoused with Muqali.

sentences.zh: 遷兵馬都鎮撫，從取大同、雁門、石、隰等州，悉平之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander-and-Pacifier of Horse and Army, followed in the taking of Datong, Yanmen, Shi, Xi, and other prefectures, and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commander-and-Pacifier of Horse and Army and helped capture Datong, Yanmen, Shi, Xi, and other prefectures, reducing them all.

sentences.zh: 引兵掠太原、平陽、河中、京兆諸城，所向款附。

translations.literal: He led troops in sweeping Taiyuan, Pingyang, Hezhong, Jingzhao, and other cities; wherever he went, submission followed.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army through Taiyuan, Pingyang, Hezhong, Jingzhao, and other cities; wherever he marched, towns submitted.

sentences.zh: 木華黎錄其功，表實為元帥左監軍。

translations.literal: Muqali recorded his merit and memorialized to appoint Shi Left Supervisor of the Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali credited his achievements and recommended him as Left Supervisor of the Marshal.

sentences.zh: 癸未，木華黎卒，子孛魯嗣。

translations.literal: In guiwei Muqali died and his son Bolu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In guiwei Muqali died, and his son Bolu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 武仙復叛，據邢。

translations.literal: Wu Xian rebelled again and held Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian rebelled again and seized Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 實帥師五千圍之，立雲梯，先士卒登堞，橫槊突之，城破，武仙走，逐北四十里，大破之，斬首二百餘級，是夜，仙黨遁去。

translations.literal: Shi commanded five thousand troops in the siege, raised scaling ladders, went ahead of the soldiers to mount the battlements, thrust horizontally with his spear into the city; the city fell, Wu Xian fled; pursuing north forty li, he broke them completely, beheading more than two hundred; that night Wu Xian's faction fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Shi besieged the city with five thousand men. He had scaling ladders raised and was first over the wall, spear leveled as he charged inside. The city fell and Wu Xian fled. Shi pursued north for forty li and routed the enemy, taking more than two hundred heads. That night Wu Xian's followers dispersed.

sentences.zh: 實下令，敢有擅剽掠者斬，軍中肅然，士民按堵。

translations.literal: Shi issued an order: whoever dared to plunder without authorization would be beheaded; the army became orderly, and soldiers and civilians lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shi ordered that unauthorized looting was punishable by death. The army kept strict discipline, and the people lived undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 孛魯命戍于邢，多著善政，邢民敬之如神明。

translations.literal: Bolu ordered him to garrison at Xing; he achieved many good policies, and the people of Xing revered him like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Bolu posted him at Xingzhou, where he governed well; the people of Xing revered him as if he were divine.

sentences.zh: 甲申，孛魯征西夏，以實分兵攻汴、陳、蔡、唐、鄧、許、鈞、睢、鄭、亳、潁，所至有功，計梟首一千五百餘級，俘工匠七百餘人。

translations.literal: In jiashen Bolu campaigned against Western Xia and had Shi divide troops to attack Bian, Chen, Cai, Tang, Deng, Xu, Jun, Sui, Zheng, Bo, and Ying; wherever he went he had merit, totaling more than fifteen hundred heads displayed and more than seven hundred artisans captured.
translations.idiomatic: In jiashen Bolu marched against Western Xia and sent Shi with detached columns against Bian, Chen, Cai, Tang, Deng, Xu, Jun, Sui, Zheng, Bo, and Ying. He won success wherever he fought, taking more than fifteen hundred heads and capturing more than seven hundred artisans.

sentences.zh: 孛魯復命駐兵邢州，分織匠五百戶，置局課織。

translations.literal: Bolu again ordered him to station troops at Xingzhou, apportioned five hundred weaving artisan households, and established a bureau to levy weaving production.
translations.idiomatic: Bolu then ordered him back to Xingzhou, allocated five hundred weaving households, and set up an office to supervise textile production.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，賜金虎符，便宜行元帥府事，邢因武仙之亂，歲屢饑，請移匠局于博，孛魯從之。

translations.literal: In dinghai he was granted a gold tiger tally and authority to act at discretion in marshal's bureau affairs; because Xing suffered repeated famine from Wu Xian's rebellion, he requested moving the artisan bureau to Bo, and Bolu approved.
translations.idiomatic: In dinghai he received a gold tiger tally and discretionary authority over the marshal's bureau. Xingzhou had suffered famine year after year since Wu Xian's revolt, so he asked to move the artisan bureau to Bo; Bolu agreed.

sentences.zh: 憫其勞瘁，使勿出征，更檄東平嚴實，與之分治軍民事。

translations.literal: Pitying his fatigue, Bolu had him exempt from campaigns and further sent orders to Dongping's Yan Shi to divide with him the governance of military and civilian affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned for his exhaustion, Bolu excused him from further campaigns and ordered Yan Shi of Dongping to share civil and military administration with him.

sentences.zh: 博值兵火後，物貨不通，實以絲數印置會子，權行一方，民獲貿遷之利。

translations.literal: Bo, having suffered from warfare and fire, saw goods and commerce blocked; Shi set up huizi notes stamped with quantities of silk, letting them circulate locally, and the people gained the benefit of trade.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars, Bo's markets had collapsed. Shi issued local notes backed by silk and kept them in circulation, restoring trade and easing the people's livelihood.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，有旨收諸將金符。

translations.literal: In gengyin there was an order to collect the gold tallies of the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In gengyin an imperial order came to recall the generals' gold tallies.

sentences.zh: 乙未，孛魯以實子仲澤為質子。

translations.literal: In yiwei Bolu took Shi's son Zhongze as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In yiwei Bolu took Shi's son Zhongze as a hostage prince.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，太宗數召入見，實貢金幣紋綺三篚。

translations.literal: In dingyou Taizong repeatedly summoned him for audience; Shi presented three cases of gold, coins, and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: In dingyou Taizong repeatedly summoned him to court, and Shi presented three cases of gold, coin, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 次陵州，遇寇，實與左右射之，斃二十餘人，生獲十餘人。
