translations.literal: Halting at Lingzhou, he encountered bandits; Shi and his attendants shot at them, killing more than twenty and capturing more than ten alive.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingzhou he was ambushed by bandits. Shi and his escorts shot back, killing more than twenty and taking more than ten alive.

sentences.zh: 朝于幄殿，帝歡甚，問遇盜之故，命所獲寇勿殺，仍以賜實。

translations.literal: At audience in the imperial tent-palace the emperor was very pleased, asked the reason for meeting the robbers, ordered the captured bandits not killed, and again bestowed them on Shi.
translations.idiomatic: At court in the imperial tent the emperor was delighted. When he asked about the ambush, he ordered the captives spared and presented them to Shi as a gift.

sentences.zh: 是日，賜坐，與論軍中故事，良久，曰：「思卿效力有年，朕欲授以征行元帥，後當重任。」

translations.literal: That day he was granted a seat and spoke of old military affairs for a long time, saying, "Reflecting that you have served devotedly for years, I wish to appoint you Campaign Marshal—you will bear heavy responsibility hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: That day he was given a seat and they talked at length of old campaigns. The emperor said, "You have served me well for many years. I mean to make you Campaign Marshal, with great duties ahead."

sentences.zh: 實叩頭謝曰︰「小臣被堅執銳，從事鋒鏑二十餘年，身被十餘槍，右臂不能舉，已為廢人矣。

translations.literal: Shi kowtowed and declined: "Your petty servant wore armor and wielded sharp weapons, engaged in the clash of blades for more than twenty years, was struck by more than ten spears, cannot raise his right arm, and is already a ruined man.
translations.idiomatic: Shi kowtowed and refused: "Your servant has worn armor and fought in the front ranks for more than twenty years. I have taken more than ten spear wounds; my right arm will not lift. I am good for nothing now.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢辱命。

translations.literal: Your servant dares not disgrace the commission.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not accept so great a charge.

sentences.zh: 願辭監軍之職，幸得元佩金符，督治工匠，歲獻織幣，優游以終其身，於臣足矣。」

translations.literal: I wish to resign the supervisor's post, and if fortunate to receive the primary girded gold tally, supervise and govern artisans, offer woven tribute yearly, and pass my remaining years at ease—that would suffice for your servant."
translations.idiomatic: I ask only to leave the supervisory post, receive a gold tally as chief overseer of artisans, submit woven tribute each year, and live out my days in peace. That would be enough for me."

sentences.zh: 帝默然不悅，令射以觀其強弱，實不能射。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent and displeased, ordered archery to observe his strength, and Shi could not shoot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent, displeased, and ordered him to shoot to test his strength. Shi could not draw the bow.

sentences.zh: 命入宿衛，密使人覘之，實臂果不能舉。

translations.literal: He was ordered into palace guard service; secretly agents were sent to observe him, and Shi's arm indeed could not be raised.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to palace guard duty while agents were secretly sent to watch him. Shi's arm truly would not lift.

sentences.zh: 固辭十餘，始可其奏。

translations.literal: After more than ten firm refusals, his memorial was at last approved.
translations.idiomatic: Only after he refused ten times over did the court accept his request.

sentences.zh: 遂錫宴，取金符親賜之，授以漢字宣命，充御用局人匠達魯花赤，子孫世其爵。

translations.literal: Then a banquet was bestowed; the gold tally was taken and personally granted; he was given a Chinese-script commission, made darughachi of the Imperial Bureau of Artisans, and his descendants inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: A feast followed. The emperor personally handed him the gold tally and issued a Chinese commission appointing him darughachi of the Imperial Artisans Bureau—a post his descendants were to inherit.

sentences.zh: 更賜白貂帽、減鐵繫腰、貂衣一襲、弓一、矢百，遣歸。

translations.literal: He was further granted a white sable hat, iron belt-clasp, one sable robe, one bow, and a hundred arrows, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given a white sable hat, an iron belt clasp, a sable robe, a bow, and a hundred arrows, then sent home.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，卒于博。

translations.literal: In dingsi he died at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In dingsi he died at Bo.

sentences.zh: 子九人，孫十七人。

translations.literal: He had nine sons and seventeen grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: He left nine sons and seventeen grandsons.

sentences.zh: 子崇禮，授應奉翰林文字、從仕郎、同知制誥兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: His son Chongli was appointed Hanlin Drafting Attendant, Junior Service Gentleman, Associate Director of Edicts, and Compiler of the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongli was made Hanlin Drafting Attendant, Junior Service Gentleman, Associate Director of Edicts, and Compiler at the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 郝和尚拔都

translations.literal: Haoheshangbadou
translations.idiomatic: Haoheshangbadou

sentences.zh: 郝和尚拔都，太原人，以小字行。

translations.literal: Haoheshangbadou was a man of Taiyuan and went by his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Haoheshangbadou was from Taiyuan and was known by his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 幼為蒙古兵所掠，在郡王迄忒麾下，長通譯語，善騎射。

translations.literal: Seized by Mongol troops in childhood, he served under Prince Qite; grown, he knew interpreter speech and was skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Captured by Mongol soldiers as a boy, he grew up in the household of Prince Qite, mastered the interpreters' languages, and became adept at horse and bow.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使宋，往返數四，以辯稱。

translations.literal: When Taizu sent envoys to Song, he went back and forth several times and was renowned for eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu dispatched envoys to the Song, he made the journey repeatedly and earned renown for his eloquence.

sentences.zh: 歲戊子，以為九原府主帥，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the wuzi year he was made commander of Jiuyuan Prefecture and bore a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuzi year he was appointed commander of Jiuyuan Prefecture with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，率兵南伐，略地潼、陝，有功。

translations.literal: In gengyin he led troops south in campaign, seized territory in Tong and Shan, and performed merit.
translations.idiomatic: In gengyin he led a southern campaign, captured territory in Tong and Shan, and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，授行軍千戶。

translations.literal: In xinmao he was appointed campaign thousand-household commander.
translations.idiomatic: In xinmao he was made a campaign thousand-household commander.

sentences.zh: 乙未，從皇子南伐，至襄陽，宋兵四十萬逆戰漢水上。

translations.literal: In yiwei he followed the imperial prince on the southern campaign to Xiangyang; four hundred thousand Song troops met them in battle on the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: In yiwei he followed an imperial prince south to Xiangyang, where four hundred thousand Song soldiers blocked them on the Han River.

sentences.zh: 領先鋒數百人，直前衝其陣，宋兵大潰。

translations.literal: Leading several hundred vanguard men, he charged straight into their formation and the Song army broke completely.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of several hundred vanguard troops he drove straight into the enemy line, and the Song army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 丙申，從都元帥塔海征蜀，下興元，宋將王連以重兵守劍閣。

translations.literal: In bingshen he followed Commander-in-Chief Tahai in the Shu campaign, took Xingyuan; the Song general Wang Lian held Jian'ge Pass with heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: In bingshen he marched under Commander-in-Chief Tahai into Shu, captured Xingyuan, and faced Song general Wang Lian, who held Jian'ge Pass with a large force.

sentences.zh: 乃募敢死士十二人，乘夜破關，入蜀，諸城悉下。

translations.literal: He then recruited twelve dare-to-die warriors, broke the pass by night, entered Shu, and all the cities submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted twelve volunteers for a death-or-glory assault, broke the pass by night, entered Shu, and reduced every city in their path.

sentences.zh: 明年，取夔府，抵大江，宋兵三十萬軍於南岸。

translations.literal: The next year he took Kuizhou Prefecture, reached the Great River; three hundred thousand Song troops arrayed on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took Kuizhou and reached the Yangtze, where three hundred thousand Song troops stood on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 郝和尚拔都選饒勇九人，乘輕舸先登，橫馳陣中，既出復入，宋兵不能支，由是以善戰名。

translations.literal: Haoheshangbadou selected nine fierce and brave men, boarded light boats first, rode across the formation back and forth entering and leaving again; the Song troops could not withstand it, and from this he gained the name of skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Haoheshangbadou picked nine of his fiercest men, crossed first in light boats, and charged back and forth through the enemy ranks. The Song line could not hold, and from then on he was famed as a master of war.

sentences.zh: 庚子歲，太宗於行在所命解衣數其瘡痕二十一，嘉其勞，進拜宣德西京太原平陽延安五路萬戶，易佩金虎符，以兵二萬屬之，復賜馬六騎、金錦弓鎧有差。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year at the mobile court Taizong ordered him to bare his body and count twenty-one scar wounds, praised his labors, promoted him to commander of ten thousand households of the five circuits Xuande, Xijing, Taiyuan, Pingyang, and Yan'an, exchanged for a gold tiger tally, assigned twenty thousand troops, and further bestowed six horses, gold brocade, bow, and armor each in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: In gengzi, at campaign headquarters, Taizong had him strip and counted twenty-one scars on his body. Praising his long service, he promoted him to ten-thousand-household commander over the five circuits of Xuande, Xijing, Taiyuan, Pingyang, and Yan'an, replaced his tally with a gold tiger tally, placed twenty thousand troops under his command, and granted six horses plus gold, brocade, bow, and armor in due measure.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，朝定宗於宿瓮都之行宮，賜銀萬鋌，辭以「賞過厚，臣不應獨受，臣得效微勞，皆將校協力之功」，遂奏將校劉天祿等十一人，皆賜之金銀符。

translations.literal: In jiachen he attended Dingzong at the traveling palace of Suwendo; ten thousand ingots of silver were bestowed; he declined: "The reward is too generous; your servant should not accept alone—whatever small service I rendered was the joint achievement of officers and commanders," then memorialized eleven officers including Liu Tianlu, all granted gold and silver tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In jiachen he presented himself to Dingzong at the Suwendo palace and was awarded ten thousand ingots of silver. He declined: "This reward is too great for me alone. Any merit I earned belongs to my officers as well." He then named eleven commanders, including Liu Tianlu, and each received a gold or silver tally.

sentences.zh: 戊申，奉詔還治太原，請凡遠道租稅監課過重者，悉蠲除之。

translations.literal: In wushen, obeying an edict he returned to govern Taiyuan and requested that all excessive land-tax supervision and levies on distant routes be entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In wushen he returned by imperial order to govern Taiyuan and petitioned for the remission of oppressive tax levies on distant districts.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，出白金六十鋌、粟千石、羊數千，以助國用。

translations.literal: In a famine year he contributed sixty ingots of white silver, a thousand shi of grain, and several thousand sheep to aid state use.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine he donated sixty ingots of silver, a thousand shi of grain, and several thousand sheep to help supply the state.

sentences.zh: 己酉，陞萬戶府為河東北路行省，得以便宜從事，凡四年。

translations.literal: In jiyou the ten-thousand-household office was elevated to the Hedong North Circuit Branch Secretariat; he was empowered to act at discretion—for four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In jiyou his ten-thousand-household command was upgraded to the Hedong North Circuit Branch Secretariat, with discretionary authority, which he held for four years.

sentences.zh: 壬子三月，卒。

translations.literal: In the third month of renzi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of renzi.

sentences.zh: 追贈太保、儀同三司、冀國公，諡忠定。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Grand Mentor, equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies, Duke of Ji State; posthumous title Loyal and Settled.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Grand Mentor, accorded third-rank honors, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with the posthumous name Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 子十二人：長天益，佩金符，太原路軍民萬戶都緫管；

translations.literal: He had twelve sons: the eldest Tianyi bore a gold tally and was Commander-in-Chief of civil and military ten thousand households of Taiyuan Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons. The eldest, Tianyi, bore a gold tally as Commander-in-Chief of civil and military affairs of the Taiyuan ten-thousand-household command;

sentences.zh: 次仲威，襲五路萬戶；

translations.literal: next Zhongwei inherited the five-circuit ten-thousand-household command;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei, the second, inherited the five-circuit ten-thousand-household post;

sentences.zh: 扎剌不花，鎮蠻都元帥、軍民宣慰使；

translations.literal: Zhala Buhua, Marshal of Zhenman Capital, Pacification Commissioner of civil and military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhala Buhua served as Marshal of Zhenman Capital and Pacification Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 天舉，大都路緫管，兼府尹；

translations.literal: Tianju, Prefect of Dadu Circuit, concurrently Prefectural Governor;
translations.idiomatic: Tianju was Prefect of Dadu Circuit and concurrently Prefectural Governor;

sentences.zh: 天祐，陝西奧魯萬戶；

translations.literal: Tianyou, ten-thousand-household commander of the ortogh of Shaanxi;
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou was ten-thousand-household commander of the Shaanxi ortogh;

sentences.zh: 天澤，夔州路緫管；

translations.literal: Tianze, Prefect of Kuizhou Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Tianze, Prefect of Kuizhou Circuit;

sentences.zh: 天麟，京兆等路諸軍奧魯萬戶；

translations.literal: Tianlin, ten-thousand-household commander of the ortogh of the various armies of Jingzhao and other circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin was ten-thousand-household commander of the Jingzhao ortogh forces;

sentences.zh: 天挺，河南江北行中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: Tingting, Pingzhang of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tingting rose to Pingzhang of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙瑨，雲中蔚州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Jin was a man of Yunzhong's Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin was from Weizhou in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 父昆，仕金為帥府評事。

translations.literal: His father Kun served the Jin as an assessor in the marshal's bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kun served the Jin as an assessor in the marshal's bureau.

sentences.zh: 兄珪，以萬戶守飛狐城。

translations.literal: His elder brother Gui held Feihu City as ten-thousand-household commander.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Gui held Feihu City as a ten-thousand-household commander.

sentences.zh: 歲庚午，昆卒，珪輦其母如蠡州，留瑨於飛狐。

translations.literal: In the gengwu year Kun died; Gui escorted their mother to Lizhou and left Jin at Feihu.
translations.idiomatic: In gengwu their father Kun died. Gui took their mother to Lizhou and left Jin at Feihu.

sentences.zh: 瑨自幼不羈，閑習武事。

translations.literal: Jin from youth was unrestrained and practiced military affairs in leisure.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Jin was wild-spirited and trained himself in arms.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，太祖南伐，先鋒至飛狐，城中不知所為。

translations.literal: In guiyou Taizu campaigned south; the vanguard reached Feihu and the city did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: In guiyou Taizu marched south. When the vanguard reached Feihu, the city was paralyzed with indecision.

sentences.zh: 瑨詣縣曰：「大兵壓境，不降何待！」

translations.literal: Jin went to the county magistrate and said, "Great armies press the borders—if not submit, what are you waiting for!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin went to the county magistrate and said, "The Mongols are at the gates. What point is there in delay?"

sentences.zh: 衆從之。

translations.literal: The crowd followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The people agreed, and the city submitted.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，太師、國王木華黎駐兵桓州，署為百戶，從攻蠡州。

translations.literal: In dingchou Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali stationed troops at Huanzhou, appointed him a hundred-household commander, and he followed in the attack on Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In dingchou Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali camped at Huanzhou, appointed him a hundred-household commander, and took him against Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 金兵閉城拒守，國王裨將石抹也先戰死，王怒，將屠其城，瑨泣曰：「母與兄在城中，乞以一身贖一城之命。」

translations.literal: Jin troops shut the city and refused defense; the prince's lieutenant Shimoyexian died in battle; the prince was angry and was about to massacre the city; Jin wept and said, "My mother and elder brother are in the city—I beg to ransom one city's lives with my own body."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin garrison barred the gates. Prince Muqali's lieutenant Shimoyexian was killed in the assault, and the prince, enraged, prepared to slaughter the city. Jin wept and pleaded: "My mother and brother are inside. Let my life redeem the whole city."

sentences.zh: 哀懇切至，國王義而許之。

translations.literal: His grief and plea were utmost; the prince, moved by righteousness, consented.
translations.idiomatic: His appeal was so heartfelt that the prince, honoring his plea, spared the city.

sentences.zh: 從攻相州，抵其門，死士突出，瑨直前擊之，流矢中鼻側，鏃出腦後，拔矢再戰，七日破其城。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Xiangzhou, reaching its gate, death-or-glory men burst out; Jin charged straight ahead to strike them; a stray arrow hit the side of his nose and the point came out behind his head; he pulled the arrow and fought again; in seven days the city was broken.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Xiangzhou he reached the gate when enemy dare-to-die troops sallied forth. He charged to meet them and took an arrow through the side of his nose—the point emerging at the back of his head. He pulled it out and fought on, and the city fell in seven days.

sentences.zh: 論功，授冀州行軍都元帥，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: Assessing merit, he was appointed Campaign Commander-in-Chief of Jizhou and bore a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief of Jizhou with a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 瑨讓其兄珪，朝廷從之，改授瑨軍民緫管，稍遷易州達魯花赤，佩金符。

translations.literal: Jin yielded the post to his elder brother Gui; the court approved, changed Jin's appointment to civil and military commander, and gradually transferred him to darughachi of Yizhou with a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: Jin yielded the post to his elder brother Gui, and the court agreed. Jin was instead made civil and military commander, later promoted to darughachi of Yizhou with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 太宗下河南，瑨自易州馳驛輸矢二十餘萬至行在，帝大喜，命權中都省事。

translations.literal: When Taizong descended on Henan, Jin from Yizhou rode post-horses to deliver more than two hundred thousand arrows to the mobile court; the emperor was greatly pleased and ordered him to act in the affairs of the Zhongdu Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong marched into Henan, Jin rushed from Yizhou by post relay with more than two hundred thousand arrows for the imperial camp. The emperor was delighted and made him provisional administrator of the Zhongdu Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，趙、揚據興州叛，瑨進軍平之，遷中山、真定二路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In guisi Zhao and Yang held Xingzhou in rebellion; Jin advanced troops and pacified it, and was transferred to darughachi of the Zhongshan and Zhending circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In guisi Zhao and Yang seized Xingzhou and rebelled. Jin marched against them and restored order, then was made darughachi of the Zhongshan and Zhending circuits.

sentences.zh: 秉溫，事世祖潛邸，命受學於太保劉秉忠，從征吐蕃、雲南大理。

translations.literal: Bingwen served Kublai's princely household; he was ordered to study under Grand Mentor Liu Bingzhong and followed campaigns against Tibet, Yunnan, and Dali.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bingwen served Kublai while he was still heir apparent. Ordered to study under Grand Mentor Liu Bingzhong, he campaigned in Tibet, Yunnan, and Dali.

sentences.zh: 中統初，詔行右三部事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong an edict had him administer the affairs of the three right departments.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhongtong era he was ordered to oversee the three right departments.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，創習朝儀，閱試稱旨，授尚書禮部侍郎、知侍儀司事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan he pioneered practice of court ritual; the review pleased the emperor; he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites of the Ministry and charged with the Ceremonial Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh Zhiyuan year he helped establish court ceremonial. When the rehearsal met imperial approval, he was made Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Ceremonial Service.

sentences.zh: 明年，授祕事少監，購求天下祕書。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Junior Supervisor of Secret Affairs and sent to purchase secret books throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Junior Supervisor of Secret Affairs and was charged with acquiring rare books throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遷昭文館大學士、知太史院侍儀司事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall of Literary Brilliance and charged with the Astronomical Bureau and Ceremonial Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Hall of Literary Brilliance and put in charge of both the Astronomical Bureau and the Ceremonial Service.

sentences.zh: 授時曆成，賜鈔二百錠，進階中奉大夫。

translations.literal: When the Shoushi Calendar was completed he was granted two hundred ingots of paper money and advanced to Grand Master of Central Submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shoushi Calendar was finished, he received two hundred ingots of paper money and was promoted to Grand Master of Central Submission.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，編國朝集禮成，帝特命其子慧襲侍儀使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, when compilation of the Collected Rites of the Dynasty was completed, the emperor specially ordered his son Hui to inherit the post of Ceremonial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, when the Collected Rites of the Dynasty was completed, the emperor ordered his son Hui to inherit the office of Ceremonial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，贈金紫光祿大夫、司徒、雲國公，諡文昭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of Education, Duke of Yun State; posthumous title Cultured and Bright.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Huangqing year he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of Education, and Duke of Yun, with the posthumous name Cultured and Illustrious.

sentences.zh: 子慧，後仕至昭文館大學士。

translations.literal: His son Hui later served up to Grand Academician of the Hall of Literary Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui later rose to Grand Academician of the Hall of Literary Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 石抹明安

translations.literal: Shimomingan
translations.idiomatic: Shimomingan

sentences.zh: 石抹明安，桓州人。

translations.literal: Shimomingan was a man of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shimomingan was a native of Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，不拘小節。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous and mild, and did not concern himself with minor points of etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature generous and easygoing, untroubled by minor proprieties.

sentences.zh: 為童子時，嘗騎杖為馬，令群兒前導，行列整肅，無敢喧譁者，父老見而異之，曰：「是兒體貌不凡，進退有度，他日必貴。」

translations.literal: When he was a child, he once rode a staff as though it were a horse and had the other children go before as guides; their ranks were orderly and disciplined, and none dared make a clamor. The village elders who saw this were struck by it and said, "This boy's bearing is extraordinary and his comings and goings have proper measure; one day he will attain high rank."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he once pretended a staff was a horse and had the other children march ahead as his escort—their lines were crisp and no one dared raise a shout. The elders who saw it marveled and said, "This child has an uncommon presence and measures his steps; he will rise high one day."

sentences.zh: 既長，歎曰：「士生于世，當立功名、書竹帛，以傳無窮，寧肯碌碌無聞，與草木同腐邪！」

translations.literal: When he had grown up, he sighed and said, "A gentleman born into the world ought to establish merit and fame and have his name written on bamboo and silk to be transmitted without end—how could he willingly live in obscurity and rot away like grass and trees!"
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he sighed and said, "A man born into this world should win glory and have his deeds set down in the histories to live forever—who would choose to pass unnoticed and moulder like grass and wood?"

sentences.zh: 歲壬申，太祖率師攻破金之撫州，將遂南向，金主命招討紇石烈九斤來援，時明安在其麾下，九斤謂之曰：「汝嘗使北方，素識蒙古國主，其往臨陣，問以舉兵之由，不然即詬之。」

translations.literal: In the year renshen the Taizu led his army in breaking Jin's Fuzhou and was about to press southward. The Jin ruler ordered Pacification Commissioner Heishilie Jiuqin to come to the rescue. At that time Ming'an was under his command. Jiuqin said to him, "You have once been envoy to the north and are well acquainted with the Mongol ruler—go out before the battle line and ask the reason for raising troops; if not, then revile him."
translations.idiomatic: In the renshen year Taizu smashed Jin's Fuzhou and prepared to march south. The Jin emperor sent Pacification Commissioner Heishilie Jiuqin to relieve the situation. Ming'an served under him at the time. Jiuqin told him, "You have been envoy to the north and know the Mongol ruler well—ride to the front and ask why he has taken up arms; if he will not answer, revile him instead."

sentences.zh: 明安初如所教，俄策馬來降，帝命縛以俟戰畢問之。

translations.literal: Ming'an at first did as instructed; soon he spurred his horse and came over in surrender. The Emperor ordered him bound until the battle should end and then questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an began as he was told, then suddenly wheeled his horse and defected. The Emperor had him bound to await questioning after the battle.

sentences.zh: 既敗金兵，召明安詰之曰：「爾何以詈我而後降也？」

translations.literal: After the Jin army was defeated, he summoned Ming'an and interrogated him, saying, "Why did you revile me before surrendering?"
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin force was broken, the Emperor called Ming'an before him and demanded, "Why did you curse me before you came over?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣素有歸志，向為九斤所使，恐其見疑，故如所言。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject has long harbored the wish to submit. Just now I was sent by Jiuqin; I feared he would become suspicious, and so I spoke as I was told.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have long wished to submit. Jiuqin had ordered me out; I feared he would suspect me if I did otherwise, so I spoke as he bid.

sentences.zh: 不爾，何由瞻奉天顏？」

translations.literal: Otherwise, by what means could I have beheld the Imperial countenance?"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise how could I ever have looked upon your face?"

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，釋之，命領蒙古軍，撫定雲中東西兩路。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved of his words, released him, and ordered him to command Mongol troops and pacify the eastern and western circuits of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased with his answer, freed him, and put him in command of Mongol forces to pacify eastern and western Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 既而帝欲休兵於北，明安諫曰：「金有天下一十七路，今我所得，惟云中東西兩路而已，若置不問，待彼成謀，併力而來，則難敵矣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Emperor wished to halt the army in the north. Ming'an remonstrated, saying, "Jin has seventeen circuits throughout the realm; what we now hold is only the eastern and western circuits of Yunzhong. If we leave the rest unattended and wait until they finish their plans and come with combined strength, we will be hard put to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor soon wanted to rest the army in the north. Ming'an urged against it: "Jin rules seventeen circuits; we hold only Yunzhong east and west. If we ignore the rest while they gather their forces and strike together, we will be overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 且山前民庶，久不知兵，今以重兵臨之，傳檄可定，兵貴神速，豈宜猶豫！」

translations.literal: Moreover, the people south of the mountains have long been unacquainted with warfare; if we now press them with a heavy army, a proclamation can settle them. In warfare speed is prized—how can we hesitate!"
translations.idiomatic: And the people beyond the mountains have hardly seen war in years—a heavy force and a written summons could bring them in at once. Speed is everything in war—why delay!"

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 即命明安引兵南進，所至，民皆具簞食壺漿以迎，盡有河北諸郡而還。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Ming'an to lead troops southward. Wherever he went, the people all brought out baskets of food and jars of drink to welcome him; he took all the commanderies of Hebei and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ming'an south at once. Everywhere the people came out with food and drink to greet him. He secured the Hebei commanderies and marched back.

sentences.zh: 帝復命明安及三合拔都，將兵由古北口徇景、薊、檀、順諸州。

translations.literal: The Emperor again ordered Ming'an and Sanhebadu to lead troops through Gubeikou and sweep the prefectures of Jing, Ji, Tan, and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then ordered Ming'an and Sanhebadu to march through Gubeikou and subdue Jing, Ji, Tan, and Shun prefectures.

sentences.zh: 諸將議欲屠之，明安奏曰：「此輩當死，今若生之，則彼之未附者，皆聞風而自至矣。」

translations.literal: The generals debated whether to slaughter them. Ming'an memorialized, "These people deserve death, but if we spare them now, then those who have not yet submitted will all hear the news and come of their own accord."
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to massacre them. Ming'an argued, "They deserve death—but if we let them live, every holdout will hear of it and surrender on his own."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 乙亥春正月，取通州，金右副元帥蒲察七斤，以其衆降，明安命復其職，置之麾下，遂駐軍于京南建春宮。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the yihai year they took Tongzhou. The Jin Right Vice Marshal Pucha Qijin surrendered with his troops. Ming'an ordered his former post restored and placed him under his command, then encamped south of the capital at Jianchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, yihai, they seized Tongzhou. Jin's Right Vice Marshal Pucha Qijin submitted with his men. Ming'an reinstated him and kept him in his own command, then encamped south of the capital at Jianchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 金御史中丞李英、元帥左都監烏古論慶壽，領兵護軍食，以援中都。

translations.literal: The Jin Censor-in-Chief Li Ying and Left Commander-in-Chief Wugulun Qingshou led troops to escort army provisions in relief of Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Censor-in-Chief Li Ying and Left Commander-in-Chief Wugulun Qingshou marched to convoy army grain to relieve Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 帝遣右副元帥神撒，將四百騎迎戰，明安將五百騎繼之，遇于永清，將戰，命士卒佯敗，金兵來追，迴擊，大破之，死及溺水者甚衆，獲李英及所佩虎符，得糧千餘車。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Right Vice Marshal Shensa with four hundred horsemen to meet them in battle; Ming'an followed with five hundred horsemen. They encountered them at Yongqing. As battle was about to begin, he ordered his soldiers to feign defeat. The Jin troops pursued; he wheeled about and struck, routing them thoroughly. Those killed and drowned were very numerous. Li Ying and the tiger tally he wore were captured, and more than a thousand carts of grain were taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Right Vice Marshal Shensa with four hundred cavalry to intercept them; Ming'an followed with five hundred. At Yongqing, on the eve of battle, he ordered his men to feign retreat. When the Jin force pursued, he swung about and crushed them—many were killed or drowned. Li Ying was taken along with his tiger tally, and they seized more than a thousand grain carts.

sentences.zh: 遂招諭永清，不降，拔而屠之。

translations.literal: He then summoned Yongqing to submit; when they did not surrender, he stormed and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: He called on Yongqing to yield; when it refused, he stormed it and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金將完顏合住、監軍阿興鬆哥，復以步兵萬二千人、糧車五百兩援中都。

translations.literal: Before long the Jin generals Wanyan Hezhu and Superintendent A-xing Songge again came with twelve thousand foot soldiers and five hundred grain carts to relieve Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, Jin generals Wanyan Hezhu and Superintendent A-xing Songge marched again with twelve thousand infantry and five hundred grain wagons to relieve Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 明安復將三千騎往擊之，遇于涿州宣封寨，獲鬆哥，合住遁去，盡得其輜重，還屯建春宮。

translations.literal: Ming'an again led three thousand horsemen to attack them. They met at Xuanfeng Stockade in Zhuozhou. Songge was captured and Hezhu fled; all their baggage was taken, and they returned to encamp at Jianchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an rode out again with three thousand cavalry and met them at Xuanfeng Stockade near Zhuozhou. Songge was captured, Hezhu escaped, and they seized the entire supply train before returning to Jianchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 四月，攻萬寧宮，克之；

translations.literal: In the fourth month they attacked Wanning Palace and took it;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they stormed Wanning Palace and took it;

sentences.zh: 取富昌、豐宜二關，攻拔固安縣。

translations.literal: They took the two passes of Fuchang and Fengyi and stormed and captured Gu'an County.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the Fuchang and Fengyi passes and captured Gu'an County.

sentences.zh: 初，順州之破，兵士縛密雲主簿完顏壽孫以獻，明安釋而用之，不久，逸去復來，問其故，對曰：「有老父在城中，恐不能存，謀歸，欲得侍養，今已歿，故復來。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shunzhou was taken, soldiers bound the Miyun Registrar Wanyan Shousun and presented him as a captive. Ming'an released him and employed him. Before long he fled away and then returned. When asked the reason, he replied, "I had an aged father in the city and feared he could not survive; I plotted to return to be able to serve and support him. He has now died, and so I have come back."
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzhou fell, soldiers had bound Miyun Registrar Wanyan Shousun and brought him in. Ming'an freed him and put him to use. He soon slipped away and then returned. Asked why, he said, "My old father was still in the city and I feared for his life. I went back to care for him. He has since died, so I have returned."

sentences.zh: 明安義而釋之。

translations.literal: Ming'an approved of his conduct and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an admired his filial duty and let him go.

sentences.zh: 五月，明安將攻中都，金相完顏復興飲藥死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, as Ming'an was about to attack Zhongdu, the Jin chancellor Wanyan Fuxing drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, as Ming'an prepared to assault Zhongdu, Jin Chancellor Wanyan Fuxing took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，城中官屬父老緇素，開門請降，明安諭之曰：「負固不服，以至此極，非汝等罪，守者之責也。」

translations.literal: On xinyou the officials, elders, monks, and laity of the city opened the gates and requested surrender. Ming'an instructed them, "Your stubborn refusal to submit has brought things to this extremity; it is not your fault—it is the fault of those who held the walls."
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the city's officials, elders, clergy, and common people opened the gates and sought surrender. Ming'an told them, "Your stubborn defense brought you to this pass—the fault lies with those who held the walls, not with you."

sentences.zh: 悉令安業，仍以粟賑之，衆皆感悅。

translations.literal: He ordered them all to resume their occupations and moreover distributed grain as relief; the multitude were all moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He let everyone return to their livelihoods and distributed grain among them; the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 明安早從軍旅，料敵制勝，筭無遺策，雖祁寒盛暑，未嘗不與士卒均勞逸，同甘苦。

translations.literal: Ming'an had long followed the army; in estimating the enemy and achieving victory his plans were never in error. Even in bitter cold or blazing heat he never failed to share hardship and ease with his soldiers and partake of the same joys and sorrows.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an had soldiered from youth onward. He read the enemy flawlessly and never missed a stratagem. Through freezing winter and scorching summer he always shared the soldiers' labors and hardships.

sentences.zh: 其得金府庫珠玉錦綺，明安悉具其數上進，未嘗以纖毫為己有。

translations.literal: When he obtained pearls, jade, brocades, and silks from Jin treasuries, Ming'an fully listed their numbers and forwarded them upward; never did he keep the slightest portion for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin treasuries yielded pearls, jade, brocade, and silk, he inventoried every piece and sent it up—never keeping so much as a thread for himself.

sentences.zh: 中都既下，加太傅、邵國公，兼管蒙古漢軍兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: After Zhongdu had fallen, he was promoted to Grand Tutor and Duke of Shao State, and concurrently placed in charge of the Grand Marshal commanding Mongol and Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongdu fell he was made Grand Tutor and Duke of Shao, with overall command of Mongol and Han forces.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以疾卒于燕城，年五十三。

translations.literal: In bingzi he died of illness in Yancheng at the age of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingzi year he died of illness in Yan at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 子二人：長咸得不，襲職為燕京行省。

translations.literal: He had two sons: the elder Xiandebude inherited the post as the Branch Secretariat of Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons—the elder, Xiandebude, inherited his office as head of the Yanjing Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 次忽篤華，太宗時，為金紫光祿大夫、燕京等處行尚書省事，兼蒙古漢軍兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: The younger, Huduhua, in the time of Taizong served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Administrator of the Branch Secretariat of Yanjing and other places, and concurrently Grand Marshal of Mongol and Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: The younger, Huduhua, under Taizong served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, head of the Yanjing Branch Secretariat, and Grand Marshal of Mongol and Han forces.

sentences.zh: 張榮字世輝，濟南歷城人，狀貌奇偉。

translations.literal: Zhang Rong, courtesy name Shihui, was a man of Licheng in Jinan; his stature and appearance were remarkably imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong, courtesy name Shihui, was from Licheng in Jinan—a man of striking size and presence.

sentences.zh: 嘗從軍，為流矢貫眥，拔之不出，令人以足抵其額而拔之，神色自若。

translations.literal: Once while serving in the army he was pierced through the corner of the eye by a stray arrow; it could not be pulled out, so he had a man brace his forehead with a foot while it was extracted, and his expression remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Once in battle a stray arrow drove through the corner of his eye. When it would not come free, he had a man pin his head with a foot and yank the shaft out—his face never changed.

sentences.zh: 金季，山東群盜蜂起，榮率鄉民據濟南黌堂嶺，衆稍盛，遂略章丘、鄒平、濟陽、長山、辛市、蒲臺、新城及淄州之地而有之，兵至，則清野入山。

translations.literal: In the final years of Jin, bandits rose everywhere in Shandong. Rong led the villagers to hold Huangtang Ridge in Jinan. His following gradually grew, and he soon overran and held the territories of Zhangqiu, Zouping, Jiyang, Changshan, Xinshi, Putai, Xincheng, and Zizhou. When enemy troops arrived, he practiced scorched earth and withdrew into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's last years bandits swarmed across Shandong. Rong rallied his neighbors on Huangtang Ridge outside Jinan, gathered strength, and seized Zhangqiu, Zouping, Jiyang, Changshan, Xinshi, Putai, Xincheng, and Zizhou. Whenever an army marched against him, he stripped the land bare and retreated into the hills.

sentences.zh: 歲丙戌，東平、順天皆內屬，榮遂舉其兵與地，納款於按赤台那衍，引見太祖，問以孤軍數載，獨抗王師之故，對曰：「山東地廣人稠，悉為帝有。

translations.literal: In the year bingxu both Dongping and Shuntian submitted to the inner territories. Rong thereupon offered up his troops and territory and yielded allegiance to A-chitanaiyan. He was brought before the Taizu, who asked the reason he had alone resisted the imperial army for years with a solitary force. He replied, "Shandong is broad in territory and densely populated—all of it belongs to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: In bingxu, as Dongping and Shuntian submitted, Rong surrendered his troops and territory to A-chitanaiyan and was presented to Taizu. Asked why he had held out alone for years against the imperial armies, he said, "Shandong is broad and populous—and all of it is yours.

sentences.zh: 臣若但有倚恃，亦不款服。」

translations.literal: If your subject had had anyone to rely upon, I would not have submitted willingly either."
translations.idiomatic: If I had had anyone left to lean on, I would never have yielded."

sentences.zh: 太祖壯之，拊其背曰：「真賽因八都兒也。」

translations.literal: The Taizu admired him and clapped him on the back, saying, "A true sa'in bagatur!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was impressed and slapped his back: "A true sa'in bagatur!"

sentences.zh: 授金紫光祿大夫、山東行尚書省，兼兵馬都元帥，知濟南府事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Administrator of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, concurrently Grand Marshal, and given charge of Jinan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, head of the Shandong Branch Secretariat and Grand Marshal, with charge of Jinan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時貿易用銀，民爭發墓劫取，榮下令禁絕。

translations.literal: At the time trade used silver, and the people competed in opening graves and plundering them. Rong issued orders strictly forbidding this.
translations.idiomatic: Trade then ran on silver, and people were robbing graves to get it. Rong outlawed the practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，朝廷集諸侯議取汴，榮請先六軍以清蹕道，帝嘉之，賜衣三襲，詔位諸侯上。

translations.literal: In gengyin the court assembled the feudatory lords to deliberate on taking Bian. Rong requested to lead the vanguard six armies to clear the imperial route. The Emperor commended him, granted three sets of robes, and by edict ranked him above the feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: In gengyin the court gathered the princes to plan the conquest of Bian. Rong volunteered to lead the vanguard and clear the imperial route. The Emperor praised him, granted three sets of robes, and ranked him above the other feudatories.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，軍至河上，榮率死士宵濟，守者潰。

translations.literal: In xinmao the army reached the river. Rong led dare-to-die troops across by night; the defenders collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In xinmao the army reached the Yellow River. Rong took picked men across by night and broke the defenders.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，敵兵整陣至，榮馳之，望風披靡，奪戰船五十艘，麾抵北岸，濟師，衆軍繼進，乘勝破張、盤二山寨，俘獲萬餘，大將阿朮魯恐生變，欲盡殺之，榮力爭而止。

translations.literal: At dawn the enemy army came up in formed ranks. Rong galloped at them; they scattered at the sight of him. He seized fifty war vessels, commanded them to the north bank, and crossed his army; the main forces followed and pressed forward. Riding victory, he broke the two mountain strongholds of Zhang and Pan, capturing more than ten thousand. Grand General Azhulu feared they might turn mutinous and wished to kill them all; Rong strenuously argued and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the enemy came in battle order. Rong charged them and they broke at once. He seized fifty warboats, ferried his men to the north bank, and the main army followed. Pressing the advantage he stormed the Zhang and Pan mountain strongholds and took more than ten thousand captives. Grand General Azhulu, fearing trouble, wanted to slaughter them all; Rong fought hard to prevent it.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，汴梁下，從阿朮魯為先鋒，攻睢陽，議欲殺俘虜，烹其油以灌城，又力止之。

translations.literal: In guisi Bianliang fell. Following Azhulu as vanguard, he attacked Suiyang. Some proposed killing the captives and boiling their fat to pour on the city; again he forcefully stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: In guisi Bian fell. Serving as Azhulu's vanguard he besieged Suiyang. When others proposed boiling captives for fat to pour on the walls, he again blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 既而城下，榮單騎入城撫其民。

translations.literal: When the city soon fell, Rong entered alone on horseback to reassure the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the city surrendered, he rode in alone to reassure the populace.

sentences.zh: 甲午，攻沛，沛拒守稍嚴，其將唆蛾夜來擣營，榮覺之，唆蛾返走，率壯士追殺之，乘勝急攻，城破。

translations.literal: In jiawu he attacked Pei. Pei's defense was somewhat stiff. Its general Suo'e came by night to raid the camp. Rong detected it; Suo'e turned and fled. He led stalwart warriors in pursuit and killed him, then pressing victory delivered a fierce assault and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In jiawu he attacked Pei, where defense was fierce. General Suo'e raided the camp by night, but Rong caught him in the act. Suo'e fled; Rong chased him down with picked men and killed him, then stormed the city at once and broke through.

sentences.zh: 就攻徐州，守將國用安引兵突出，榮逆擊之，亦破其城，用安赴水死。

translations.literal: He then attacked Xuzhou. The defending general Guo Yong'an led troops in a sortie; Rong met them head-on, likewise broke the city, and Yong'an threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to Xuzhou. Defender Guo Yong'an led a breakout charge; Rong met him head-on, stormed the city, and Yong'an drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 乙未，拔邳州。

translations.literal: In yiwei he took Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In yiwei he captured Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 丙申，從諸王闊端破宋棗陽、仇城等三縣。

translations.literal: In bingshen he followed Prince Kuoduan in breaking the three counties of Zaoyang, Qiucheng, and others in Song territory.
translations.idiomatic: In bingshen he followed Prince Kuoduan in capturing three Song counties including Zaoyang and Qiucheng.

sentences.zh: 時河南民北徙至濟南，榮下令民間，分屋與地居之，俾得樹畜，且課其殿最，曠野辟為樂土。

translations.literal: At the time people of Henan who had migrated north reached Jinan. Rong issued orders among the populace to allot houses and land for them to dwell, enabling them to plant crops and raise livestock, and moreover assessed their achievements so that the wasted wilderness was opened up into a land of peace and plenty.
translations.idiomatic: Henan refugees were flooding into Jinan. Rong had households share houses and land so they could farm and keep livestock, graded their progress, and turned empty fields into thriving settlements.

sentences.zh: 是歲，中書考績，為天下第一。

translations.literal: That year in the assessment of achievements by the Central Secretariat, his was ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Central Secretariat's performance review ranked him first in the empire.

sentences.zh: 李璮據益都，私餽以馬蹄金，榮曰：「身既許國，何可擅交鄰境！」

translations.literal: Li Tan held Yidu and privately sent him horse-hoof gold as a gift. Rong said, "Having pledged my person to the state, how can I privately deal with a neighboring territory!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Tan of Yidu sent him horse-hoof gold as a private gift. Rong refused: "My loyalty is to the throne—how can I trade favors with a neighboring lord?"

sentences.zh: 却之。

translations.literal: He refused it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent it back.

sentences.zh: 年六十一，乞致仕，後十九年，世祖即位，封濟南公，致仕卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: At sixty-one he requested retirement from office. Nineteen years later, when Shizu took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jinan. He died in retirement at the age of eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty-one he retired. Nineteen years later, when Shizu ascended the throne, he was made Duke of Jinan. He died in retirement at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 子七人：長邦傑，襲爵，先卒；

translations.literal: He had seven sons: the eldest Bangjie inherited the title and died first;
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons—the eldest, Bangjie, inherited his title but died before him;

sentences.zh: 邦直，行軍萬戶；

translations.literal: Bangzhi, Field Army Myriarch;
translations.idiomatic: Bangzhi, Field Army Myriarch;

sentences.zh: 邦彥，權濟南行省；

translations.literal: Bangyan, Acting Administrator of the Jinan Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan, Acting Administrator of the Jinan Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 邦允，知淄州；

translations.literal: Bangyun, Prefect of Zizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Bangyun, Prefect of Zizhou;

sentences.zh: 邦孚，大都督府郎中；

translations.literal: Bangfu, Attendant of the Grand Military Council;
translations.idiomatic: Bangfu, Attendant of the Grand Military Council;

sentences.zh: 邦昌，奧魯緫管；

translations.literal: Bangchang, A'uru Commander;
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang, A'uru Commander;

sentences.zh: 邦憲，淮安路緫管。

translations.literal: Bangxian, Prefect of the Huai'an Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian, Prefect of the Huai'an Circuit.

sentences.zh: 孫四十人，宏，襲邦傑爵，改真定路緫管。

translations.literal: He had forty grandsons. Hong inherited Bangjie's title and was changed to Prefect of the Zhending Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had forty grandsons. Hong inherited Bangjie's title and became Prefect of the Zhending Circuit.

sentences.zh: 劉亨安

translations.literal: Liu Hengan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hengan

sentences.zh: 劉亨安，其先范陽人，後遷遼東川州。

translations.literal: Liu Hengan—his ancestors were men of Fanyang; later they moved to Chuanzhou in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hengan was descended from men of Fanyang who later settled in Chuanzhou, Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 初，國王木華黎經略遼東，兄世英率宗族鄉人隸麾下，分兵收燕、趙、雲、朔、河東，以功充行軍副緫管。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Prince Muqali was conducting operations in Liaodong, his elder brother Shiying led clan members and fellow villagers to attach themselves to his command, divided forces to take Yan, Zhao, Yun, Shuo, and Hedong, and on merit was installed as Vice Administer of the Field Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Muqali was pacifying Liaodong, his elder brother Shiying brought clan and neighbors into Muqali's service. Shiying sent detachments to take Yan, Zhao, Yun, Shuo, and Hedong, and for his merit was made Vice Administer of the Field Army.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，平陽諸郡被兵之餘，民物空竭，世英言於王曰：「自古建國，以民為本，今河東殺掠殆盡，異日我師復來，孰給轉輸？

translations.literal: In gengchen, after the Pingyang commanderies had suffered warfare, the people and goods were utterly exhausted. Shiying said to the Prince, "Since ancient times the founding of a state has taken the people as its foundation. Now Hedong has been slaughtered and plundered almost to extinction; if another day our army comes again, who will supply transport?
translations.idiomatic: In gengchen, after war had ravaged the Pingyang region, people and goods were exhausted. Shiying told the prince, "Every state is built on its people. Hedong has been stripped bare—when our armies return, who will feed the supply lines?

sentences.zh: 收存恤亡，此其時也。」

translations.literal: To gather in the living, preserve them, and succor the perishing—this is the time for it."
translations.idiomatic: Now is the time to shelter the living and restore what war has destroyed."

sentences.zh: 王善之。

translations.literal: The Prince approved.
translations.idiomatic: The prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 以絳州邊地，難其人，奏授世英絳州節度使，兼行帥府事。

translations.literal: Because Jiangzhou was a frontier district and hard to find the right man for, he memorialized to appoint Shiying Military Commissioner of Jiangzhou, concurrently acting on behalf of the Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou was a frontier post and hard to fill—he recommended Shiying as Military Commissioner of Jiangzhou with authority of the Marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 卒于師，無子，國王孛魯命其族兄德仁襲職。

translations.literal: He died in the army and had no son. Prince Belu ordered his clansman elder brother Deren to inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: He died on campaign without a son. Prince Belu had his kinsman Deren inherit the office.

sentences.zh: 丙戌歲，金將移剌副樞攻絳州，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: In the year bingxu the Jin general Yelü Vice Cavalry Commander attacked Jiangzhou; the city fell and he died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In bingxu Jin general Yelü the Vice Cavalry Commander attacked Jiangzhou. The city fell and Deren died defending it.

sentences.zh: 木華黎承制命亨安領其衆，奏賜金虎符，授鎮國上將軍、絳州節度使，行元帥府事，兼觀察使。

translations.literal: Muqali, acting by imperial commission, ordered Hengan to take command of his troops. He memorialized to grant a golden tiger tally and appointed him General Who Stabilizes the State, Military Commissioner of Jiangzhou, acting on behalf of the Marshal's headquarters, and concurrently Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali, acting on imperial authority, put Hengan in command of Deren's troops. He was granted a golden tiger tally and made General Who Stabilizes the State, Military Commissioner of Jiangzhou, with authority of the Marshal's headquarters and the concurrent post of Observation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庚寅冬，從王師渡河入關。

translations.literal: In the winter of gengyin he followed the princely army in crossing the river and entering the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of gengyin he crossed the Yellow River with the imperial army and entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 辛卯春，克鳳翔，歷秦、隴，屯渭陽。

translations.literal: In the spring of xinmao he took Fengxiang, passed through Qin and Long, and encamped at Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of xinmao he captured Fengxiang, marched through Qin and Long, and encamped at Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 秋，出階城，沿漢抵鄧。

translations.literal: In autumn he went out from Jie Prefecture, followed the Han River, and reached Deng.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he marched from Jie Prefecture down the Han River to Deng.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，會大軍於鈞州，敗金人於三峰山。

translations.literal: In renchen he joined the main army at Junzhou and defeated the Jin at Sanfeng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In renchen he joined the main force at Junzhou and helped rout the Jin at Sanfeng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 甲午，平蔡。

translations.literal: In jiawu he pacified Cai.
translations.idiomatic: In jiawu he helped pacify Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而宋兵二十萬攻汴，將趨洛，都元帥塔察兒俾亨安往拒之，與宋軍遇龍門北，遂橫槊躍馬，奮突而前，衆因乘之，宋師奔潰，追擊百餘里，塔察兒拊其背曰：「真驍將也。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward two hundred thousand Song troops attacked Bian and were about to press toward Luoyang. Grand Marshal Tachar had Hengan go to resist them. He encountered the Song army north of Longmen, then levelled his spear, spurred his horse, and charged fiercely forward; the troops thereupon pressed the advantage, and the Song army fled in rout. They pursued for more than a hundred li. Tachar clapped him on the back and said, "A true fierce general!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, two hundred thousand Song troops attacked Bian and marched toward Luoyang. Grand Marshal Tachar sent Hengan to block them. North of Longmen he levelled his spear, spurred forward, and charged. His men surged after him and the Song army broke. They pursued for more than a hundred li. Tachar slapped his back and said, "A true fighting general!"

sentences.zh: 延坐諸將之右，勞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: He had him seated to the right of the generals and rewarded him with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He seated him above the other generals and rewarded him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 丙申，都元帥塔海征巴蜀，攻散關，破劍門，出奇制勝，戰功居多。

translations.literal: In bingshen Grand Marshal Tahai campaigned in Ba-Shu. He attacked Sanguan, broke Jianmen, achieved victory through unexpected stratagems, and Hengan's share of the battle merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In bingshen Grand Marshal Tahai campaigned in Ba-Shu. Hengan fought at Sanguan, broke through Jianmen, and won with daring maneuvers—his share of the credit was the largest.

sentences.zh: 進圍成都，亨安為先鋒，大破之於城西，生擒宋將陳侍郎。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Chengdu, Hengan served as vanguard and routed them greatly west of the city, capturing alive the Song general Vice Minister Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When they besieged Chengdu, Hengan led the vanguard and routed the defenders west of the city, taking Vice Minister Chen of Song alive.

sentences.zh: 有喬長官與亨安爭功，未幾，攻城，喬為砲所傷，亨安負之以出，喬感愧。

translations.literal: There was a Director Qiao who disputed merit with Hengan. Before long, during the assault on the city, Qiao was wounded by a catapult; Hengan carried him out on his back, and Qiao was moved to shame and gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Director Qiao had quarreled with him over credit. During the assault Qiao was struck by a catapult stone; Hengan carried him out on his back, and Qiao was overcome with shame and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 亨安從軍十年，累著勳伐，所獲金帛，悉推與將佐，故士卒咸樂為用。

translations.literal: Hengan followed the army for ten years and repeatedly achieved distinguished merit. The gold and silks he obtained he entirely passed on to his officers and aides, and therefore the soldiers all gladly served under him.
translations.idiomatic: Hengan soldiered for ten years and won repeated distinction. He gave every coin and bolt of silk to his officers, and his men served him willingly.

sentences.zh: 癸卯冬十二月卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter of guimao he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of winter, guimao.

sentences.zh: 子貞，嗣職。

translations.literal: His son Zhen inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited his office.

sentences.zh: 孫三人：弘，彊，弴。

translations.literal: He had three grandsons: Hong, Qiang, and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three grandsons: Hong, Qiang, and Dan.
